title.zh: 卷一百五十七 列傳第四十五 金純 張本 郭敦 郭璡 鄭辰 柴車 劉中敷 張鳳 周瑄 楊鼎 黃鎬 胡拱辰 陳俊 林鶚 潘榮 夏時正
title.en: Volume 157 Biographies 45: Jin Chun, Zhang Ben, Guo Dun, Guo Jin, Zheng Chen, Chai Che, Liu Zhongfu, Zhang Feng, Zhou Xuan, Yang Ding, Huang Gao, Hu Gongchen, Chen Jun, Lin E, Pan Rong, Xia Shizheng

sentences.zh: 金純 張本 郭敦 郭璡 鄭辰 柴車 劉中敷 孫機 張鳳 周瑄 子紘 楊鼎 翁世資 黃鎬 胡拱辰 陳俊 林鶚 潘榮 夏時正

translations.literal: Jin Chun, Zhang Ben, Guo Dun, Guo Jin, Zheng Chen, Chai Che, Liu Zhongfu, Sun Ji, Zhang Feng, Zhou Xuan, [his] son Hong, Yang Ding, Weng Shizi, Huang Gao, Hu Gongchen, Chen Jun, Lin E, Pan Rong, Xia Shizheng
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chun, Zhang Ben, Guo Dun, Guo Jin, Zheng Chen, Chai Che, Liu Zhongfu, Sun Ji, Zhang Feng, Zhou Xuan, his son Hong, Yang Ding, Weng Shizi, Huang Gao, Hu Gongchen, Chen Jun, Lin E, Pan Rong, and Xia Shizheng

sentences.zh: 金純，字德修，泗州人。

translations.literal: Jin Chun, styled Dexiu, was a man of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chun, whose courtesy name was Dexiu, came from Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武中國子監生。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he was a student at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongwu emperor he studied at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書杜澤薦，授吏部文選司郎中。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Du Ze, Minister of Personnel, he was appointed director of the Selection Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Du Ze, the Minister of Personnel, he was made director of the Ministry's Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三十一年出為江西布政司右參政。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he went out as right vice administrator of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one of the reign he was posted as right vice administrator of the Jiangxi provincial government.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，以蹇義薦，召為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, on Jian Yi's recommendation he was summoned and made right vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle emperor's accession, Jian Yi recommended him, and he was recalled to serve as right vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時將營北京，命采木湖廣。

translations.literal: At that time Beijing was to be built; he was ordered to procure timber in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: As the court was preparing to build Beijing, he was sent to gather timber in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年從巡北京。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle he accompanied the tour of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year seven he accompanied the imperial inspection tour of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 八年從北征，遷左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he joined the northern campaign and was promoted to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took part in the northern expedition and was promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 九年命與宋禮同治會通河，又同徐亨、蔣廷瓚浚魚王口黃河故道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered together with Song Li to supervise dredging of the Huitong Canal; he also joined Xu Heng and Jiang Tingzan in dredging the old Yellow River course at Yuwang Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was ordered to supervise dredging of the Huitong Canal together with Song Li, and also joined Xu Heng and Jiang Tingzan in dredging the old Yellow River course at Yuwang Mouth.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖用兵梁、晉間，使大將軍徐達開塌場口，通河於泗。

translations.literal: At first, when the founding emperor campaigned between Liang and Jin, he had Grand General Xu Da open Tacangkou to connect the river to the Si.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the founding emperor campaigned between Liang and Jin, he had Grand General Xu Da open Tacangkou to connect the river to the Si.

sentences.zh: 又開濟寧西耐牢坡引曹、鄆河水，以通中原之運。

translations.literal: He also opened Nailaopo west of Jining to channel the Cao and Yun River waters, linking transport to the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened Nailaopo west of Jining to channel the Cao and Yun River waters and link transport to the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 其後故道浸塞，至是純疏治之。

translations.literal: Afterward the old course gradually silted up; at this time Jin Chun dredged and restored it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the old course gradually silted up, and at this time Jin Chun dredged and restored it.

sentences.zh: 自開封北引水達鄆城，入塌場，出穀亭北十里為永通、廣運二閘。

translations.literal: Water was drawn north from Kaifeng to reach Yancheng, entering Tacang; ten li north of Guting two sluices were established, Yongtong and Guangyun.
translations.idiomatic: Water was drawn north from Kaifeng to Yancheng, entered Tacang, and ten li north of Guting the Yongtong and Guangyun sluices were built.

sentences.zh: 十四年改禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to left vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to left vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 越二月，進尚書。

translations.literal: Two months later he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 十五年從巡北京。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he accompanied the imperial tour of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he accompanied the imperial tour of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十九年同給事中葛紹祖巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he together with Supervising Secretary Ge Shaozu toured and pacified Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he toured and pacified Sichuan together with Supervising Secretary Ge Shaozu.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，改工部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 居數月，又改刑部。

translations.literal: After several months he was again transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was transferred again to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 明年兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: The next year he was additionally appointed tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was additionally appointed tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，純有疾，帝命醫視療。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande, Chun fell ill, and the emperor ordered physicians to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande, Jin Chun fell ill, and the emperor sent physicians to attend him.

sentences.zh: 稍間，免其朝參，俾護疾視事。

translations.literal: When he improved slightly, his court attendance was excused and he was allowed to nurse his illness while still handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he improved a little, he was excused from court attendance and permitted to tend his illness while continuing to manage his duties.

sentences.zh: 會暑，敕法司理滯囚。

translations.literal: It being summer, the emperor ordered the judicial offices to clear backlogged prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the emperor ordered the judicial offices to review long-detained prisoners.

sentences.zh: 純數從朝貴飲，為言官所劾。

translations.literal: Chun repeatedly drank with court nobles and was impeached by remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chun repeatedly joined senior officials for drinking parties and was impeached by the censors.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「純以疾不朝而燕於私，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily, "Chun claims illness and skips court yet feasts in private—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in anger, "Chun pleads illness to avoid court yet feasts privately—is that permissible?"

sentences.zh: 命系錦衣獄。

translations.literal: He ordered him imprisoned in the Brocade Guard jail.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jin Chun imprisoned in the Brocade Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 既念純老臣，釋之，落太子賓客。

translations.literal: Then, remembering that Chun was an old minister, he released him and demoted him from his post as tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that Jin Chun was a veteran minister, the emperor released him and stripped him of his post as tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 八月予致仕去。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was granted retirement and left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was granted retirement and left the capital.

sentences.zh: 純在刑部，仁宗嘗諭純：「法司近尚羅織，言者輒以誹謗得罪，甚無謂。

translations.literal: While Chun was at the Ministry of Justice, Emperor Renzong once instructed him, "The judicial offices lately favor fabricating charges; those who speak out are often punished for slander, which is quite pointless.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin Chun served at the Ministry of Justice, Emperor Renzong once told him, "The courts lately love to weave charges together; anyone who speaks up is punished for slander, which is absurd.

sentences.zh: 自今告誹謗者勿論。」

translations.literal: From now on, do not entertain accusations of slander."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, do not prosecute accusations of slander."

sentences.zh: 純亦務寬大，每誡屬吏不得妄椎擊人。

translations.literal: Chun likewise pursued leniency and repeatedly admonished his subordinates not to beat people recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chun likewise favored leniency and repeatedly warned his subordinates not to beat prisoners without cause.

sentences.zh: 故當純時，獄無瘐死者。

translations.literal: Therefore during Chun's tenure no one died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure, no prisoner died of neglect or mistreatment in the jails.

sentences.zh: 正統五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 贈山陽伯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Marquis of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 張本，字致中，東阿人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ben, styled Zhizhong, was a man of Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben, whose courtesy name was Zhizhong, came from Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，自國子生授江都知縣。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, as an Imperial Academy student he was appointed magistrate of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he left the Imperial Academy to become magistrate of Jiangdu county.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至揚州，御史王彬據城抗，為守將所縛。

translations.literal: When the Yan army reached Yangzhou, censor Wang Bin held the city in resistance but was bound by the defending commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army reached Yangzhou, Censor Wang Bin held the city in defiance but was seized by the garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 本率父老迎降。

translations.literal: Ben led the elders of the district to welcome them and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben led the local elders out to welcome the army and surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 成祖以滁、泰二知州房吉、田慶成率先歸附，命與本並為揚州知府，偕見任知府譚友德同涖府事。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor, because the prefects of Chuzhou and Taizhou, Fang Ji and Tian Qingcheng, had been the first to submit, ordered them together with Ben to serve jointly as prefects of Yangzhou, together with the incumbent prefect Tan Youde to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prefects of Chuzhou and Taizhou, Fang Ji and Tian Qingcheng, had been the first to submit, the Yongle emperor appointed them together with Zhang Ben as co-prefects of Yangzhou, sharing administration with the incumbent Tan Youde.

sentences.zh: 尋擢本江西布政司右參政。

translations.literal: Soon Ben was promoted to right vice administrator of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Ben was promoted to right vice administrator of the Jiangxi provincial government.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年召為工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle he was summoned as left vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year four he was recalled to serve as left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 坐事免官，冠帶辦事。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for an offense but retained his cap and sash to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense but allowed to keep his rank insignia and continue handling business.

sentences.zh: 明年五月復官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The following May his post was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋以奏牘書銜誤左為右，為給事中所劾。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because a memorial bore the wrong title—right written for left—he was impeached by a supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a memorial listed his title incorrectly as right instead of left, and a supervising secretary impeached him.

sentences.zh: 帝命改授本部右侍郎而宥其罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him reassigned as right vice minister of the same ministry and pardoned the offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassigned him as right vice minister of the same ministry and pardoned the error.

sentences.zh: 七年，皇太子監國，奏為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the crown prince was regent, he was memorialized for appointment as right vice minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven, while the crown prince governed as regent, he was appointed right vice minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 善摘奸。

translations.literal: He was skilled at exposing wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for uncovering fraud and malfeasance.

sentences.zh: 命督北河運。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise transport on the northern canal.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of grain transport on the northern canal.

sentences.zh: 躬自相視，立程度，舟行得無滯。

translations.literal: He personally inspected the route, set standards, and kept the boats moving without delay.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the route himself, set clear standards, and kept the fleet moving without backlog.

sentences.zh: 會疾作，太子賜之狐裘冠鈔，遣醫馳視。

translations.literal: When illness struck, the crown prince gave him a fox-fur robe, cap, and paper money and sent physicians posthaste.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the crown prince sent him a fox-fur robe, cap, and cash stipend and dispatched physicians at once.

sentences.zh: 十九年將北征，命本及王彰分往兩直隸、山東、山西、河南，督有司造車挽運。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, as a northern campaign was planned, Ben and Wang Zhang were sent separately to the two metropolitan areas and to Shandong, Shanxi, and Henan to supervise local offices in building carts for transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen, with a northern campaign in prospect, Zhang Ben and Wang Zhang were sent to the two metropolitan regions and to Shandong, Shanxi, and Henan to oversee local officials in building supply carts.

sentences.zh: 明年即命本督北征餉。

translations.literal: The next year Ben was immediately ordered to supervise provisions for the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put in charge of supplies for the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，拜南京兵部尚書兼掌都察院事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Ben was appointed Minister of War at Nanjing and also placed in charge of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, Zhang Ben was made Minister of War at Nanjing and given charge of the Censorate as well.

sentences.zh: 召見，言時政得失，且請嚴飭武備。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he spoke on the gains and losses of current policy and also asked that military readiness be strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he discussed what was right and wrong in current policy and urged the emperor to tighten military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之，遂留行在兵部。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted his advice and kept him at the traveling Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his counsel and retained him at the traveling Ministry of War at the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，工部侍郎蔡信乞征軍匠家口隸錦衣衛。

translations.literal: Early in Xuande, Vice Minister of Works Cai Xin requested that the households of military artisans be conscripted into the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign, Vice Minister of Works Cai Xin asked that the families of military artisans be drafted into the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 本言：「軍匠二萬六千人，屬二百四十五衛所，為匠者暫役其一丁。

translations.literal: Ben said, "There are twenty-six thousand military artisans belonging to two hundred forty-five guards and battalions; of those serving as artisans, only one man per household is temporarily levied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben replied, "There are twenty-six thousand military artisans spread across two hundred forty-five guards and battalions; only one able-bodied man per household is temporarily drafted for artisan service.

sentences.zh: 若盡取以來，家以三四丁計之，數近十萬。

translations.literal: If all were taken, counting three or four men per household, the number would approach one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: If every household member were taken, counting three or four men per family, the total would approach one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 軍伍既缺，人情驚駭，不可。」

translations.literal: The military rolls would be depleted and the people terrified; this must not be done."
translations.idiomatic: Military households would be gutted and the populace thrown into panic; this cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 帝善本言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved Ben's argument.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Zhang Ben's argument.

sentences.zh: 征漢庶人，從調兵食。

translations.literal: In the campaign against the Han prince of the blood, he followed to arrange troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against the deposed Prince of Han, he went along to organize troops and supplies.

sentences.zh: 庶人就擒，命撫輯其眾，而錄其餘黨。

translations.literal: When the prince was captured, Ben was ordered to pacify his followers and register the remaining partisans.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince was taken, he was ordered to pacify the rebel following and register any remaining partisans.

sentences.zh: 還以軍政久敝，奸人用貸脫籍，而援平民實伍，言於帝。

translations.literal: On his return he reported to the emperor that military administration had long been corrupt: scoundrels bought their way off the rolls while commoners were pressed into the ranks to fill quotas.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he told the emperor that military administration had decayed for years—corrupt men bought their way off the rolls while civilians were dragooned to fill the quotas.

sentences.zh: 擇廷臣四出厘正之。

translations.literal: Court ministers were chosen and sent out in four directions to rectify the abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor chose senior officials and sent them out in four directions to set the rolls right.

sentences.zh: 時馬大孳息，畿內軍民為畜牧所困。

translations.literal: At the time horses had multiplied greatly, and soldiers and civilians in the capital region were harried by pasturage duties.
translations.idiomatic: Horses had multiplied so greatly that soldiers and civilians around the capital were overwhelmed by pasturage obligations.

sentences.zh: 本請分牧于山東、河南及大名諸府。

translations.literal: Ben requested that herds be distributed for grazing in Shandong, Henan, and the prefectures around Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben asked that herds be distributed for grazing in Shandong, Henan, and the Daming region.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南養馬自此始。

translations.literal: Horse breeding in Shandong and Henan began from this.
translations.idiomatic: State horse breeding in Shandong and Henan began with this measure.

sentences.zh: 晉王濟熿坐不軌奪爵，本奉命散其護衛軍于邊鎮。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Ji Huang was stripped of his title for sedition; Ben was ordered to disperse his guard troops among the frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin Ji Huang was stripped of his title for treason, Zhang Ben was ordered to disperse his guard troops among the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 四年命兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to serve additionally as tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was also appointed tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 戶部以官田租減，度支不給，請減外官俸及生員軍士月給。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue, because rents from official fields had fallen and disbursements could not be met, requested cuts to the salaries of local officials and the monthly stipends of students and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Because rents from official fields had fallen short and the treasury could not cover expenses, the Ministry of Revenue asked to cut local officials' salaries and the monthly pay of students and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 帝以軍士艱，不聽減。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering the hardship of the soldiers, would not allow the reduction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of the soldiers' hardship, refused to cut their pay.

sentences.zh: 餘下廷議，本等持不可，乃止。

translations.literal: The remainder was referred to court deliberation; Ben and others held that it could not be done, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The rest was debated at court; Zhang Ben and others opposed it, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 陽武侯薛祿城獨石諸戍成，本往計守禦之宜。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Yangwu Xue Lu completed fortifying the garrisons at Dushi and elsewhere, Ben went to plan how they should be held and defended.
translations.idiomatic: After Marquis of Yangwu Xue Lu finished fortifying Dushi and the other border posts, Zhang Ben went to plan their garrison and defense.

sentences.zh: 還奏稱旨，命兼掌戶部。

translations.literal: On his return his memorial pleased the emperor, who ordered him to take charge of the Ministry of Revenue as well.
translations.idiomatic: His report on returning pleased the emperor, who also put him in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 本慮邊食不足，而諸邊比歲稔，請出絲麻布帛輸邊易穀，多者三四十萬石，少者亦十萬石，儲偫頓充。

translations.literal: Ben feared frontier grain was insufficient; since the border regions had had good harvests in successive years, he asked to send out silk, hemp, and cloth to the frontiers to exchange for grain—up to three or four hundred thousand piculs in some places and no less than one hundred thousand elsewhere—so stores were suddenly filled.
translations.idiomatic: Worried that frontier granaries were low while the border regions had enjoyed good harvests, he proposed sending silk, hemp, and cloth to exchange for grain—up to three or four hundred thousand piculs in some areas and at least one hundred thousand in others—swiftly filling the reserves.

sentences.zh: 六年病卒，賜賻三萬緡，葬祭甚厚。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died of illness; thirty thousand strings of cash were granted for funeral expenses, and burial rites were very lavish.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he died of illness; the court granted thirty thousand strings of cash for his funeral and gave him an exceptionally lavish burial.

sentences.zh: 本廉介有執持，尚刻少恕。

translations.literal: Ben was upright and principled, inclined to severity and sparing of forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben was incorruptible and firm in principle, inclined toward severity and slow to forgive.

sentences.zh: 錄高煦黨，脅從者多不免。

translations.literal: When the partisans of Zhu Gaoxu were registered, many who had been coerced could not escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Gaoxu's followers were prosecuted, many who had been coerced were punished nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 成祖宴近臣，銀器各一案，因以賜之。

translations.literal: The Yongle Emperor feasted his close ministers; each had a tray of silver vessels, which he then bestowed on them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle emperor entertained his close ministers, setting a tray of silver vessels before each and then giving them away as gifts.

sentences.zh: 獨本案設陶器，諭曰：「卿號『窮張』，銀器無所用。」

translations.literal: Only before Ben's place stood pottery; the emperor said, "You are called 'Poor Zhang'; silver would be of no use to you."
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Ben's place held pottery; the emperor said, "You are called 'Poor Zhang'—silver would be wasted on you."

sentences.zh: 本頓首謝，其為上知如此。

translations.literal: Ben kowtowed in thanks; such was the emperor's understanding of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben kowtowed in thanks—such was the emperor's intimate knowledge of him.

sentences.zh: 郭敦，字仲厚，堂邑人。

translations.literal: Guo Dun, styled Zhonghou, was a man of Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Dun, whose courtesy name was Zhonghou, came from Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以鄉舉入太學，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, on a provincial recommendation he entered the Imperial University and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he entered the Imperial University on a provincial recommendation and was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷衢州知府，多惠政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Quzhou, where he enacted many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Quzhou, where he carried out many policies that benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 衢俗，貧者死不葬，輒焚其屍。

translations.literal: The custom in Quzhou was that when the poor died and could not be buried, their corpses were simply burned.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom in Quzhou was that when the poor died without means for burial, their bodies were cremated instead.

sentences.zh: 敦為厲禁，且立義阡，俗遂革。

translations.literal: Dun strictly forbade this and also established a public burial ground, and the custom was reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Dun strictly forbade the practice and established a public burial ground, and the custom was changed.

sentences.zh: 禁民聚淫祠。

translations.literal: He forbade the people to gather at illicit shrines.
translations.idiomatic: He also banned gatherings at unauthorized shrines.

sentences.zh: 敦疾，民勸弛其禁，弗聽，疾亦瘳。

translations.literal: When Dun fell ill, the people urged him to relax the ban; he would not listen, and his illness also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the people urged him to lift the ban; he refused, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 在衢七年。

translations.literal: He was in Quzhou seven years.
translations.idiomatic: He served seven years in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，坐累征，耆老數百人伏闕乞留，不得。

translations.literal: Early in Yongle he was summoned to the capital because of an implicated offense; several hundred elders prostrated themselves at the palace gate begging that he be kept, but to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he was recalled to the capital on a related charge; several hundred elders knelt at the palace gate begging that he stay, but their plea was denied.

sentences.zh: 後廷臣言敦廉正，召補監察御史。

translations.literal: Later court officials reported that Dun was upright; he was recalled and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when court officials praised his integrity, he was recalled and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 遷河南左參政，調陝西。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left vice administrator of Henan and then transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice administrator of Henan and then transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十六年春，胡濙言敦有大臣體，擢禮部右侍郎兼太僕寺卿，偕給事中陶衎巡撫順天。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year, Hu Ying said Dun had the bearing of a great minister; he was promoted to right vice minister of Rites and concurrently director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and together with supervising secretary Tao Kan was sent to tour and pacify Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year sixteen, Hu Ying said Guo Dun had the stature of a great minister; he was made right vice minister of Rites and concurrent director of the Imperial Stud, and with Supervising Secretary Tao Kan was sent to oversee Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十年督北征餉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he supervised provisions for the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty he supervised supplies for the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，以大行喪不齋宿，降太僕卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, because Guo Dun had not observed fasting and abstinence during the grand mourning rites, he was demoted from director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, Guo Dun was demoted from director of the Imperial Stud for failing to observe fasting and abstinence during the grand mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 旋進戶部左侍郎，兼詹事府少詹事。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to left vice minister of Revenue and concurrently appointed vice director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left vice minister of Revenue and concurrent vice director of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 陝西旱，命與隆平侯張信整飭庶務當行者，同三司官計議奏行。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi suffered drought, he was ordered together with Marquis Zhang Xin of Longping to set in order all current administrative tasks requiring action, and together with the three provincial commissioners to deliberate and memorialized for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi suffered drought, he was ordered with Marquis Zhang Xin of Longping to put current administrative tasks in order and, together with the three provincial commissioners, to deliberate and memorialized what should be done.

sentences.zh: 敦乃請蠲逋賦，振貧乏，考黜貪吏，罷不急之務，凡十數事。

translations.literal: Guo Dun then requested remission of overdue taxes, relief for the poor, review and dismissal of corrupt officials, and abolition of non-urgent tasks—more than ten measures in all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Dun then proposed more than ten measures: remitting overdue taxes, relieving the poor, reviewing and dismissing corrupt officials, and abolishing non-urgent tasks.

sentences.zh: 悉從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召還。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 在部多所興革，罷王田之奪民業者，令民開荒不起科。

translations.literal: At the ministry he instituted many reforms: he abolished princely estates that had seized civilian holdings, and ordered that people who reclaimed wasteland would not be taxed on it initially.
translations.idiomatic: At the ministry he instituted many reforms, abolishing princely estates that had seized commoners' land and ordering that newly reclaimed wasteland would not be taxed at first.

sentences.zh: 建漕運議，民運至瓜洲、儀真，資衛卒運至京。

translations.literal: He proposed a grain transport plan whereby civilians would transport grain to Guazhou and Yizhen, and garrison troops would then carry it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a transport plan under which civilians would haul grain to Guazhou and Yizhen and garrison troops would carry it on to the capital.

sentences.zh: 民甚便之。

translations.literal: The people found this very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people found the arrangement greatly convenient.

sentences.zh: 敦事親孝，持身廉。

translations.literal: Dun was filial toward his parents and kept himself incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Dun was devoted to his parents and scrupulously honest in his conduct.

sentences.zh: 同官有為不義者，輒厲色待之，其人悔謝乃已。

translations.literal: When colleagues acted unjustly, he would treat them sternly until they repented and apologized, and only then would he relent.
translations.idiomatic: When colleagues behaved unjustly, he confronted them sternly until they repented and apologized, and only then would he relent.

sentences.zh: 性好學，公退，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning; after leaving public duties his hand never left his books.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning by nature and, after office hours, never set his books aside.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒官，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in office at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he died in office at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 郭璡，字時用，初名進，新安人。

translations.literal: Guo Jin, styled Shiyong, originally named Jin, was a man of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin, whose courtesy name was Shiyong and whose original name was Jin, came from Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，乙太學生擢戶部主事。

translations.literal: Early in Yongle, as a second-class graduate of the Imperial University he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle, as a second-class graduate of the Imperial University he was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 曆官吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as left and right vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，命兼詹事府少詹事，更名璡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was ordered to serve concurrently as vice director of the Household of the Heir Apparent and changed his name to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, he was made concurrent vice director of the Heir Apparent's household and changed his name to Jin.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，掌行在詹事府。

translations.literal: Early in Xuande he was placed in charge of the traveling Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he headed the traveling household of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蹇義老，輟部務，帝欲以璡代。

translations.literal: Jian Yi, Minister of Personnel, was aged and had set aside ministry affairs; the emperor wished to replace him with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Jian Yi was elderly and had stepped back from daily duties; the emperor intended to replace him with Guo Jin.

sentences.zh: 璡厚重勤敏，然寡學術。

translations.literal: Jin was solid, diligent, and quick, yet shallow in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin was steady, diligent, and capable, but lacked scholarly depth.

sentences.zh: 楊士奇言恐璡不足當之，宜妙擇大臣通經術知今古者，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Yang Shiqi said he feared Jin might not be equal to the post and that a minister well versed in the classics and knowing past and present should be carefully chosen; the emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shiqi warned that Guo Jin might not be equal to the post and urged the emperor to choose a minister steeped in the classics and versed in past and present affairs; the emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒為尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he nevertheless became minister.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made minister after all.

sentences.zh: 諭以呂蒙正夾袋，虞允文材館錄故事。

translations.literal: He was instructed in the stories of Lü Mengzheng's talent pouch and Yu Yunwen's roster of men of ability.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him the stories of Lü Mengzheng's talent pouch and Yu Yunwen's roster of capable men.

sentences.zh: 璡由是留意人才。

translations.literal: Jin thereafter paid attention to men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Guo Jin paid close attention to identifying talent.

sentences.zh: 識進士李賢輔相器，授吏部主事，後果為名相。

translations.literal: He recognized in the jinshi Li Xian the makings of a chief minister, appointed him a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and Li later indeed became a famous prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: He recognized in the jinshi Li Xian the makings of a chief minister, appointed him a principal clerk in Personnel, and Li later became one of the great ministers of the age.

sentences.zh: 時外官九年考滿，部民走闕下乞留，輒增秩復任。

translations.literal: At that time, when local officials completed their nine-year term, the people of the department would rush to the capital to beg that they be kept, and they were routinely promoted in rank and reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, when local officials finished their nine-year review, the people of their jurisdiction would rush to the capital to beg that they stay, and the court routinely promoted them and reappointed them.

sentences.zh: 璡慮有妄者，請覆實。

translations.literal: Jin feared there might be impostors and requested that the petitions be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin worried that some petitions might be fraudulent and asked that they be investigated.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 璡雖長六卿，然望輕。

translations.literal: Although Jin was senior among the six ministries, his prestige was slight.
translations.idiomatic: Although Guo Jin headed one of the six ministries, he carried little weight at court.

sentences.zh: 又政歸內閣，自布政使至知府闕，聽京官三品以上薦舉；

translations.literal: Moreover, as power had passed to the Grand Secretariat, vacancies from provincial administrators down to prefects were filled on recommendation by capital officials of the third rank and above;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with power concentrated in the Grand Secretariat, vacancies from provincial administrators down to prefects were filled on recommendations from capital officials of the third rank and above;

sentences.zh: 既又命御史、知縣，皆聽京官五品以上薦舉。

translations.literal: later it was also ordered that investigating censors and magistrates alike be appointed on recommendation by capital officials of the fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: later investigating censors and county magistrates were also appointed on recommendations from capital officials of the fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 要職選擢，皆不關吏部。

translations.literal: Selection and promotion to important posts no longer involved the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Important appointments no longer passed through the Ministry of Personnel at all.

sentences.zh: 正統初，左通政陳恭言：「古者擇任庶官，悉由選部，職任專而事體一。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengtong, Left Assistant Minister Chen Gong said, "In antiquity the appointment of all ordinary officials was entirely handled by the Selection Bureau, with concentrated responsibility and a single procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign, Left Assistant Minister Chen Gong said, "In antiquity every ordinary official was chosen through the Selection Bureau alone, with clear responsibility and a single standard.

sentences.zh: 今令朝臣各舉所知，恐開私謁之門，長奔競之風，乞杜絕，令歸一。」

translations.literal: Now, if court ministers are each to recommend those they know, I fear it will open the door to private canvassing and encourage frantic competition; I beg that this be stopped and authority restored to one channel."
translations.idiomatic: If every minister is allowed to recommend his own acquaintances, private lobbying and frantic competition will follow; I beg that this be ended and authority returned to a single channel."

sentences.zh: 下吏部議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was sent to the Ministry of Personnel for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 璡遜謝不敢當，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Jin declined humbly, saying he was unfit; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin humbly declined, saying he was unfit for the post, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，御史曹恭以災異請罷大臣不職者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, Censor Cao Gong, citing natural disasters, requested the dismissal of grand ministers who were derelict in duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, Censor Cao Gong cited omens and disasters to ask that incompetent senior ministers be removed.

sentences.zh: 帝命科道官參議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered officials of the censorate and the remonstrance bureaus to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered censors and remonstrance officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 璡及尚書吳中、侍郎李庸等被劾者二十人。

translations.literal: Jin, Minister Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Li Yong, and others—twenty men in all—were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin, Minister Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Li Yong, and others—twenty officials in all—were impeached.

sentences.zh: 璡等自陳，帝切責而宥之。

translations.literal: Jin and the others made their own statements; the emperor sternly rebuked them but pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin and the others submitted their own accounts; the emperor rebuked them sharply but pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 璡子亮受賂為人求官。

translations.literal: Jin's son Liang took bribes to secure appointments for others.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin's son Liang took bribes to obtain offices for others.

sentences.zh: 事覺，御史孫毓等劾璡。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, Censor Sun Yu and others impeached Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Censor Sun Yu and others impeached Guo Jin.

sentences.zh: 乃令璡致仕，而以王直代。

translations.literal: Jin was then ordered to retire and Wang Zhi was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jin was ordered to retire, and Wang Zhi was appointed in his stead.

sentences.zh: 鄭辰，字文樞，浙江西安人。

translations.literal: Zheng Chen, styled Wenshu, was a man of Xi'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen, whose courtesy name was Wenshu, came from Xi'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年進士，授監察御史。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Yongle, he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination in Yongle year four, he was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 江西安福民告謀逆事，命辰往廉之，具得誣狀。

translations.literal: When the people of Anfu in Jiangxi reported a plot of treason, Chen was ordered to investigate and fully established that the charge was false.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Anfu in Jiangxi reported a treason plot, Zheng Chen was sent to investigate and proved the accusation entirely false.

sentences.zh: 福建番客殺人，復命辰往。

translations.literal: When foreign merchants in Fujian killed a man, Chen was again ordered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign merchants in Fujian committed murder, he was again sent to handle the case.

sentences.zh: 止坐首惡，釋其餘。

translations.literal: He punished only the ringleader and released the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He punished only the ringleader and released the others.

sentences.zh: 南京敕建報恩寺，役囚萬人。

translations.literal: At Nanjing the emperor ordered the building of the Bao'en Temple, employing ten thousand convict laborers.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing the emperor ordered construction of the Bao'en Temple, using ten thousand convict laborers.

sentences.zh: 蜚語言役夫謗訕，恐有變，命辰往驗。

translations.literal: Rumors said the laborers were slandering the project and might rebel; Chen was ordered to verify the reports.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that the laborers were slandering the work and might revolt; Zheng Chen was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 無實，無一得罪者。

translations.literal: There was no truth in it, and not one man was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The rumors proved groundless, and not a single laborer was punished.

sentences.zh: 谷庶人謀不軌，復命辰察之，盡得其蹤跡。

translations.literal: When the commoner Gu plotted sedition, Chen was again ordered to investigate and traced the affair completely.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed Prince Gu plotted rebellion, Zheng Chen was again sent to investigate and uncovered the entire conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 帝語方賓曰：「是真國家耳目臣矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Fang Bin, "This is truly a minister who serves as the eyes and ears of the state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Fang Bin, "Here is a true eyes-and-ears minister of the realm."

sentences.zh: 十六年超遷山西按察使，糾治貪濁不少貸。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted out of turn to surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and prosecuted the corrupt without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he was promoted ahead of schedule to surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and prosecuted corruption without mercy.

sentences.zh: 潞州盜起，有司以叛聞，詔發兵討捕。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Luzhou; local officials reported rebellion, and an edict ordered troops sent to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Luzhou; local officials reported a rebellion, and the court ordered troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 辰方以事朝京師，奏曰：「民苦徭役而已，請無發兵。」

translations.literal: Chen happened to be in the capital on business and memorialized, "The people suffer only from corvée labor; I beg that troops not be sent."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen happened to be at court on business and memorialized, "The people suffer only from corvée burdens; I beg that no troops be sent."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 還則屏騶從，親入山谷撫諭。

translations.literal: On his return he dismissed his escort and personally entered the valleys to console and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he dismissed his escort and went personally into the hills to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 盜皆感泣，復為良民。

translations.literal: The bandits all wept in gratitude and returned to being law-abiding people.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits wept in gratitude and returned to peaceful lives.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎蔚綬轉粟給山海軍，辰統山西民輦任。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Wei Shou was transferring grain to supply the Shanhai garrison; Chen directed the people of Shanxi to carry the loads.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Rites Wei Shou arranged grain shipments for the Shanhai garrison, Zheng Chen organized the people of Shanxi to transport them.

sentences.zh: 民勞，多逋耗，綬令即山海貸償之。

translations.literal: The people were exhausted and many deliveries were short; Wei ordered that compensation be borrowed immediately from Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: The people were exhausted and many shipments fell short; Wei ordered immediate loans from Shanhai to make up the deficit.

sentences.zh: 辰曰：「山西民貧而悍，急之恐生變。

translations.literal: Chen said, "The people of Shanxi are poor and fierce; if pressed too hard they may rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen said, "The people of Shanxi are poor and fierce; pressing them too hard may provoke unrest.

sentences.zh: 不如緩之，使自通有無。」

translations.literal: It would be better to proceed gently and let them settle shortages among themselves."
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to proceed gently and let them make up shortages among themselves."

sentences.zh: 用其言，卒無逋者。

translations.literal: His advice was followed, and in the end none defaulted.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was followed, and in the end no one defaulted.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱歸，軍民詣御史乞留。

translations.literal: When he went home on mourning leave for his mother, soldiers and civilians went to the censor begging that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home to mourn his mother, soldiers and civilians petitioned the censor to keep him in office.

sentences.zh: 御史以聞，服闋還舊任。

translations.literal: The censor reported this, and when mourning was over Chen returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: The censor reported their plea, and when mourning ended Zheng Chen resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年召為南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he was summoned as right vice minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he was recalled to serve as right vice minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 初，兩京六部堂官缺，帝命廷臣推方面官堪內任者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when chief posts in the six ministries at the two capitals fell vacant, the emperor ordered court ministers to recommend provincial officials fit for appointment within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when senior posts in the six ministries at both capitals fell vacant, the emperor ordered ministers to recommend provincial officials suited for capital appointment.

sentences.zh: 蹇義等薦九人。

translations.literal: Jian Yi and others recommended nine men.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi and others recommended nine candidates.

sentences.zh: 獨辰及邵玘、傅啟讓，帝素知其名，即真授，餘試職而已。

translations.literal: Only Chen, Shao Qi, and Fu Qirang were men whose names the emperor already knew; they received full appointments at once, while the rest were given trial posts only.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zheng Chen, Shao Qi, and Fu Qirang were men the emperor already knew by reputation; they received full appointments at once, while the others were given trial posts only.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，分遣大臣考察天下方面官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, senior ministers were dispatched to inspect provincial officials throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong succeeded, senior ministers were sent out to inspect provincial officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 辰往四川、貴州、雲南，悉奏罷其不職者。

translations.literal: Zheng Chen went to Sichuan, Guizhou, and Yunnan and memorialized to dismiss all those found unfit for office.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen went to Sichuan, Guizhou, and Yunnan and memorialized to remove every official found unfit for duty.

sentences.zh: 雲南布政使周璟居妻喪，繼娶。

translations.literal: Zhou Jing, provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan, was mourning his wife yet remarried.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing, provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan, was in mourning for his wife yet remarried.

sentences.zh: 辰劾其有傷風教，璟坐免。

translations.literal: Zheng Chen impeached him for damaging public morals, and Zhou was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen impeached him for violating public morals, and Zhou was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 正統二年，奉命振南畿、河南饑。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengtong he was ordered to provide famine relief in the Southern Capital region and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengtong he was ordered to provide famine relief in the Southern Capital region and Henan.

sentences.zh: 時河堤決，即命辰伺便修塞。

translations.literal: At that time the river embankment burst, and he was immediately ordered to seize a suitable opportunity to repair the breach.
translations.idiomatic: When the river embankment burst, he was immediately ordered to repair the breach at the first suitable opportunity.

sentences.zh: 或議自大名開渠，引諸水通衛河，利灌輸。

translations.literal: Some proposed opening a canal from Daming to channel various waters into the Wei River for irrigation and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed opening a canal from Daming to channel various waters into the Wei River to aid irrigation and transport.

sentences.zh: 辰言勞民不便，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Zheng Chen said it would burden the people without benefit, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen said it would burden the people without sufficient benefit, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部左侍郎，與豐城侯李彬轉餉宣府、大同。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left vice minister of War and, together with Marquis Li Bin of Fengcheng, transported provisions to Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice minister of War and, with Marquis Li Bin of Fengcheng, transported provisions to Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 鎮守都督譚廣撓令，劾之，事以辦。

translations.literal: Tan Guang, the garrison commander, obstructed his orders; Zheng Chen impeached him, and the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Tan Guang obstructed his orders; Zheng Chen impeached him, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 八年得風疾，告歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he contracted wind paralysis and requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he contracted wind paralysis and asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died.

sentences.zh: 辰為人重義輕財。

translations.literal: Chen valued righteousness and held wealth lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen valued honor above wealth.

sentences.zh: 初登進士，產悉讓兄弟。

translations.literal: When he first passed the jinshi examination, he gave all his property to his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When he first passed the jinshi examination, he gave all his property to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 在山西與同僚杜僉事有違言。

translations.literal: While in Shanxi he had a falling-out with his colleague Vice Commissioner Du.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Shanxi he quarreled with his colleague Vice Commissioner Du.

sentences.zh: 杜卒，為治喪，資遣其妻子。

translations.literal: When Du died, Chen arranged the funeral and provided funds to send off his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Du died, Zheng Chen arranged his funeral and provided funds to send his wife and children home.

sentences.zh: 柴車，字叔輿，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chai Che, styled Shuyu, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Che, whose courtesy name was Shuyu, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，以舉人授兵部武選司主事，曆員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle, on a provincial recommendation he was appointed principal clerk in the Military Selection Bureau of the Ministry of War and rose to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year two, on a provincial recommendation he became principal clerk in the Ministry of War's Military Selection Bureau and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，從尚書方賓扈行。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the emperor campaigned north, he accompanied Minister Fang Bin on the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, when the emperor marched north, he accompanied Minister Fang Bin on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 還遷江西右參議。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to right vice administrator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made right vice administrator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 坐事，左遷兵部郎中，出知岳州府，復入為郎中。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to director in the Ministry of War, then sent out as prefect of Yuezhou, and later re-entered the ministry as director again.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to director in the Ministry of War, then sent out as prefect of Yuezhou, and later returned to the ministry as director.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande he was promoted to vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuande he was promoted to vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，山西巡按御史張勖言，大同屯田多為豪右佔據，命車往按。

translations.literal: The next year, Touring Censor of Shanxi Zhang Xu reported that much of the garrison farmland at Datong had been seized by powerful families; Che was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Shanxi touring censor Zhang Xu reported that much garrison farmland at Datong had been seized by powerful families; Chai Che was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 得田幾二千頃，還之軍。

translations.literal: He recovered nearly two thousand qing of land and returned it to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered nearly two thousand qing of land and returned it to the garrison.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，西鄙不靖。

translations.literal: Early in the Yingzong reign the western frontier was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Yingzong's reign the western frontier was unsettled.

sentences.zh: 以車廉幹，命協贊甘肅軍務。

translations.literal: Because Che was incorruptible and capable, he was ordered to assist in Gansu military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chai Che was honest and capable, he was ordered to assist in Gansu military affairs.

sentences.zh: 調軍給餉，悉得事宜。

translations.literal: In deploying troops and supplying provisions, he handled everything appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: In deploying troops and supplying provisions, he handled every matter appropriately.

sentences.zh: 初，朵兒只伯寇涼州，副總兵劉廣喪師。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Duerzhibo raided Liangzhou, Deputy Commander-in-Chief Liu Guang lost his army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Duerzhibo raided Liangzhou, deputy commander Liu Guang lost his army.

sentences.zh: 不以實聞，顧飾功要賞。

translations.literal: He did not report the truth but instead embellished his achievements to claim rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to report the truth and instead embellished his record to claim rewards.

sentences.zh: 車劾其罪，械廣至京。

translations.literal: Che impeached him for the offense and had Guang sent to the capital in the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Che impeached him and had Liu Guang sent to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 賜車金幣，旌其直。

translations.literal: Che was granted gold and coins in recognition of his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded Chai Che with gold and coins in recognition of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 岷州土官後能冒功得升賞，車奏請加罪。

translations.literal: The native official Houneng of Minzhou had falsely claimed merit and received promotion and rewards; Che memorialized asking that he be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The native official Houneng of Minzhou had falsely claimed merit and been promoted and rewarded; Chai Che memorialized asking that he be punished.

sentences.zh: 能復請，命宥之。

translations.literal: Houneng petitioned again, and an order pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Houneng petitioned again, and the emperor ordered him pardoned.

sentences.zh: 車反覆論其不可，曰：「詐冒如能者，實繁有徒，臣方次第按核。

translations.literal: Che argued repeatedly that this could not be done, saying, "False claimants like Houneng are indeed numerous; I am just beginning to investigate them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Che argued repeatedly that this could not stand, saying, "False claimants like Houneng are legion; I have only begun to investigate them systematically.

sentences.zh: 今宥能，何以戢眾？

translations.literal: If Houneng is pardoned now, how can the multitude be restrained?
translations.idiomatic: If Houneng is pardoned now, how can others be restrained?

sentences.zh: 若無功得官，則捐軀死敵者，何以待之？」

translations.literal: If men without merit receive office, how are those who gave their lives fighting the enemy to be treated?"
translations.idiomatic: If the undeserving gain office, what reward is left for those who died fighting the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖從能請，然嘉車賢，遣使勞賜之。

translations.literal: Although the court followed Houneng's petition, it praised Che's integrity and sent an envoy to console and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Although the court granted Houneng's petition, it praised Chai Che's integrity and sent an envoy to console and reward him.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，以破朵兒只伯功，增俸一級。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, for the merit of defeating Duerzhibo, his salary was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengtong, for defeating Duerzhibo, his salary was raised one grade.

sentences.zh: 在邊，章數十上，悉中時病。

translations.literal: On the frontier he submitted dozens of memorials, all striking at the ills of the time.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he submitted dozens of memorials, each striking at the problems of the day.

sentences.zh: 同事多不悅，車持益堅。

translations.literal: Many colleagues were displeased, but Che held all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Many colleagues were displeased, but Chai Che held his ground all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 嘗建言：「漠北降人，朝廷留之京師，雖厚爵賞，其心終異。

translations.literal: He once proposed, "The surrendered people of the northern desert whom the court keeps in the capital, though richly ennobled and rewarded, remain alien at heart.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed, "The northern tribesmen who surrendered and whom the court keeps in the capital, though richly ennobled and rewarded, remain alien at heart.

sentences.zh: 如長脫脫木兒者，昔隨其長來歸，未幾叛去。

translations.literal: Men such as Changtuotuomu'er once came in with their chiefs, but before long rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Changtuotuomu'er once came in with their chiefs, but soon rebelled and fled.

sentences.zh: 今乃復來，安知他日不再叛，宜徙江南，離其黨類。」

translations.literal: Now he has come again—who knows he will not rebel once more? They should be moved to the south and separated from their fellows."
translations.idiomatic: Now he has returned—who can be sure he will not rebel again? They should be resettled south of the Yangtze, far from their fellows."

sentences.zh: 事下兵部，請處之河間、德州。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of War, which requested that they be settled at Hejian and Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministry of War, which proposed resettling them at Hejian and Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 帝報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 後降者悉以此令從事。

translations.literal: Later surrenderers were all handled according to this order.
translations.idiomatic: Later surrenderers were all handled according to this policy.

sentences.zh: 稽核屯田豪占者，悉清出之，得六百餘頃。

translations.literal: In auditing garrison fields seized by powerful families, he cleared them all and recovered more than six hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: In auditing garrison farmland seized by powerful families, he recovered more than six hundred qing.

sentences.zh: 四年進兵部尚書，參贊如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Minister of War, with his assisting duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was promoted to Minister of War while continuing his assisting duties on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼理陝西屯田。

translations.literal: Soon he was also ordered to oversee garrison farmland in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also put in charge of garrison farmland in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年召還，命與僉都御史曹翼歲更代出鎮。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled and ordered to alternate yearly with Vice Censor-in-Chief Cao Yi in commanding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and ordered to alternate yearly with Vice Censor-in-Chief Cao Yi in commanding the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 及期病甚。

translations.literal: When his term came due he was gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: When his term came due he was gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 詔遣大理寺少卿程富代翼，而命車歸治疾。

translations.literal: An edict sent Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cheng Fu to replace Yi and ordered Che home to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Director Cheng Fu of the Court of Judicial Review to replace Cao Yi and ordered Chai Che home to recover.

sentences.zh: 未及行，六年六月卒。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, he died in the sixth month of the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, he died in the sixth month of year six.

sentences.zh: 車在江西時，以采木入閩，經廣信。

translations.literal: While Che was in Jiangxi, on a mission to gather timber he entered Fujian and passed through Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Jiangxi, on a timber-gathering mission he entered Fujian and passed through Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 廣信守，故人也，饋蜜一罌。

translations.literal: The prefect of Guangxin, an old acquaintance, sent him a jar of honey as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Guangxin, an old friend, sent him a jar of honey as a gift.

sentences.zh: 發視之，乃白金。

translations.literal: When he opened it and looked, it was silver.
translations.idiomatic: When he opened it, he found silver inside.

sentences.zh: 笑曰：「公不知故人矣」，卻不受。

translations.literal: He laughed and said, "You do not know your old friend," and refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed and said, "You do not know your old friend at all," and refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 同事邊塞者多以宴樂為豪舉。

translations.literal: Many colleagues on the frontier treated feasting and pleasure as grand displays.
translations.idiomatic: Many colleagues on the frontier treated feasting and revelry as marks of status.

sentences.zh: 車惡之，遂斷酒肉。

translations.literal: Che detested this and thereupon gave up wine and meat entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Che detested this and gave up wine and meat entirely.

sentences.zh: 其介特多此類。

translations.literal: His uncompromising integrity took many such forms.
translations.idiomatic: His uncompromising integrity took many such forms.

sentences.zh: 劉中敷，大興人，初名中孚。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongfu, a man of Daxing, was originally named Zhongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongfu, from Daxing, was originally named Zhongfu.

sentences.zh: 燕王舉兵，以諸生守城功，授陳留丞。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan raised troops, for his merit as a student in defending the city he was appointed assistant magistrate of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan raised troops, for his merit as a student defender of the city he was made assistant magistrate of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 擢工部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 仁宗監國，命署部事，賜今名。

translations.literal: When the crown prince governed as regent, he was ordered to handle ministry affairs and was granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince governed as regent, he was put in charge of ministry affairs and granted his present name.

sentences.zh: 遷江西右參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice administrator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice administrator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年遷山東右參政，進左布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he was transferred to right vice administrator of Shandong and then promoted to left provincial administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he was made right vice administrator of Shandong and then promoted to left provincial administrator.

sentences.zh: 質直廉靜，吏民畏懷。

translations.literal: Upright, honest, and reserved, he was feared and respected by officials and people alike.
translations.idiomatic: Upright, honest, and reserved, he was feared and respected by officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 歲大侵，言于巡撫，減賦三之二。

translations.literal: In a year of severe famine he spoke to the touring pacification commissioner and had taxes reduced by two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe famine he persuaded the touring pacification commissioner to cut taxes by two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 正統改元，父憂奪情，俄召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Zhengtong reign began, during mourning for his father he was spared leave and continued in office; soon he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengtong reign, when his father died he was allowed to remain in office rather than withdraw for mourning; soon afterward he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝沖年踐阼，慮群下欺己，治尚嚴。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the throne in his youth and feared that his subordinates would deceive him; governance tended toward severity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the throne while still very young and feared being misled by his officials, so his rule tended toward severity.

sentences.zh: 而中官王振假以立威，屢摭大臣小過，導帝用重典，大臣下吏無虛歲。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Zhen used this to establish his authority, repeatedly seizing upon minor faults of great ministers and leading the emperor to apply heavy penalties; there was scarcely a year when senior officials were not handed over to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Zhen exploited this climate to build his power, repeatedly dredging up minor offenses by senior ministers and steering the emperor toward harsh punishments; hardly a year passed without some minister being turned over to the courts.

sentences.zh: 三年諷給事御史劾中敷與左侍郎吳璽等，下獄，釋還職。

translations.literal: In the third year, supervising secretaries and censors were prompted to impeach Zhongfu together with Left Vice Minister Wu Xi and others; they were imprisoned, then released and restored to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, supervising secretaries and censors were maneuvered into impeaching Zhongfu along with Left Vice Minister Wu Xi and others; they were jailed, then released and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 六年，言官劾中敷專擅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, remonstrating officials impeached Zhongfu for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, remonstrating officials impeached Zhongfu for arrogating power to himself.

sentences.zh: 詔法司於內廷雜治。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the judicial offices to try the case jointly in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the judicial offices to hear the case jointly within the inner court.

sentences.zh: 當流，許輸贖。

translations.literal: The sentence was banishment, and payment of a redemption fine was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to banishment, with the option of paying a fine in lieu of exile.

sentences.zh: 帝特宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially granted him a pardon.

sentences.zh: 其冬，中敷、璽及右侍郎陳瑺請以供禦牛馬分牧民間。

translations.literal: That winter, Zhongfu, Xi, and Right Vice Minister Chen Kao asked that the oxen and horses kept for imperial use be distributed among the common people for grazing.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Zhongfu, Xi, and Right Vice Minister Chen Kao proposed distributing the oxen and horses reserved for the imperial household among local households for pasturing.

sentences.zh: 言官劾其變亂成法，並下獄論斬。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials impeached them for overturning established law; all were imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials accused them of overturning established law; all three were imprisoned and sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 詔荷校長安門外，凡十六日而釋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to bear the cangue outside Chang'an Gate; after sixteen days they were released.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered to wear the cangue outside Chang'an Gate and were released after sixteen days.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌入貢，詔問馬駝芻菽數，不能對，復與璽、瑺論斬系獄。

translations.literal: When the Oirats came to pay tribute, an edict asked the numbers of horses, camels, fodder, and grain; he could not answer; again, together with Xi and Kao he was sentenced to death and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Oirats came bearing tribute, the emperor asked how many horses, camels, fodder, and grain were on hand; Zhongfu could not answer. He was again condemned to death along with Xi and Kao and held in prison.

sentences.zh: 中敷以母病，特許歸省。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill, Zhongfu was specially permitted to return home to visit her.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was ill, Zhongfu was granted special leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，當決囚，法司以請。

translations.literal: The next winter, when it came time to carry out executions, the judicial offices submitted a request.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, when executions were due, the judicial offices submitted their recommendation.

sentences.zh: 命璽、瑺戍邊，中敷俟母終其奏。

translations.literal: Xi and Kao were ordered to garrison the frontier; Zhongfu was to wait until his mother's death to carry out his sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Kao were ordered to the frontier as garrison troops; Zhongfu's sentence was deferred until after his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 已，釋為民。

translations.literal: Afterward he was released and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was released and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，起戶部左侍郎兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, Zhongfu was recalled as Left Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, Zhongfu was recalled as Left Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵，論功行賞無虛日。

translations.literal: At the time troops were being deployed; rewards for merit were handed out almost every day.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was at war, and rewards for merit were dispensed nearly every day.

sentences.zh: 中敷言府庫財有限，宜撙節以備緩急。

translations.literal: Zhongfu said that treasury funds were limited and that expenditures should be restrained to prepare for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu argued that treasury resources were limited and that spending should be tightened to meet emergencies.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of minister.

sentences.zh: 中敷性淡泊，食不重味，仕宦五十年，家無餘資。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was by nature abstemious; his meals were never richly flavored. After fifty years in office, his family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu was by nature abstemious and never ate richly flavored food. After fifty years in office, his family had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 子璉，正統十年進士。

translations.literal: His son Lian passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lian passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑科給事中，累官太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed reviewing secretary in the Bureau of Punishments and rose through the ranks to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed reviewing secretary in the Bureau of Punishments and eventually rose to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 恥華靡，居官剛果。

translations.literal: He despised luxury and was firm and resolute in office.
translations.idiomatic: He despised luxury and was firm and resolute in office.

sentences.zh: 左遷遼東苑馬寺卿，卒。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Director of the Liaodong Pasturage Office and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Director of the Liaodong Pasturage Office, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子機，幼有孝行。

translations.literal: His son Ji showed filial devotion from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji was filial from childhood.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourteenth year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶起士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 正德中，代張彩為吏部尚書，以人言乞歸。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, he replaced Zhang Cai as Minister of Personnel; because of criticism he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he replaced Zhang Cai as Minister of Personnel, but after criticism from others he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 起南京兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Minister of War at Nanjing to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of War at Nanjing to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 流賊犯江上，眾議擇將。

translations.literal: When roving bandits raided along the Yangtze, the assembly debated whom to choose as general.
translations.idiomatic: When roving bandits raided along the Yangtze, officials debated whom to appoint as commander.

sentences.zh: 適都督李昴自貴州罷官至，機即召任之。

translations.literal: Just then the regional commander Li Ang, who had been dismissed from Guizhou and arrived, was immediately summoned and appointed by Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Regional Commander Li Ang, who had been dismissed from Guizhou and had arrived, was immediately summoned and appointed by Ji.

sentences.zh: 昂以無朝命辭。

translations.literal: Ang declined on the grounds that there was no imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Ang declined on the grounds that he had received no imperial order.

sentences.zh: 機曰：「機奉敕有雲，『敕所不載，聽便宜』。

translations.literal: Ji said: "In the commission I received it says, 'What the commission does not specify may be handled as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "My commission states, 'What the commission does not specify may be handled as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 此即朝命也。」

translations.literal: That is the imperial order.'
translations.idiomatic: That is the imperial order.'

sentences.zh: 眾服其膽識。

translations.literal: All admired his courage and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his courage and judgment.

sentences.zh: 致仕歸，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 張鳳，字子儀，安平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Feng, styled Ziyi, was a native of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Feng, styled Ziyi, was from Anping.

sentences.zh: 父益，官給事中。

translations.literal: His father Yi served as a supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi served as a supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年從征漠北，歿於陣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle he followed the northern campaign into the desert and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Yongle reign he joined the northern campaign into the desert and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 鳳登宣德二年進士。

translations.literal: Feng passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Feng passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 讞江西叛獄，平反數百人。

translations.literal: In hearing a rebellion case in Jiangxi, he exonerated several hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: While adjudicating a rebellion case in Jiangxi, he exonerated several hundred people.

sentences.zh: 正統三年十二月，法司坐事盡系獄，遂擢鳳本部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhengtong, when officials of the judicial offices were all imprisoned for misconduct, Feng was promoted to Right Vice Minister in the same ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhengtong, when judicial officials were all imprisoned for misconduct, Feng was promoted to Right Vice Minister in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以主事擢侍郎，前時未有也。

translations.literal: Promotion from clerk to vice minister had never happened before.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion from clerk directly to vice minister had never occurred before.

sentences.zh: 明年命提督京倉。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered to supervise the capital granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was ordered to supervise the capital granaries.

sentences.zh: 六年改戶部，尋調南京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and soon afterward to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and soon afterward to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 適尚書久闕，鳳遂掌部事。
