translations.literal: As the minister's post had long been vacant, Feng took charge of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: As the minister's post had long been vacant, Feng took charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 貴州奏軍衛乏糧，乞運龍江倉及兩淮鹽於鎮遠府易米。

translations.literal: Guizhou reported that military garrisons lacked grain and asked to transport salt from Longjiang Granary and the two Huai salterns to Zhenyuan Prefecture to exchange for rice.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou reported that military garrisons lacked grain and requested that salt from Longjiang Granary and the two Huai salterns be shipped to Zhenyuan Prefecture to exchange for rice.

sentences.zh: 鳳以龍江鹽雜泥沙，不堪易米給軍，盡以淮鹽予之，然後以聞。

translations.literal: Feng considered Longjiang salt adulterated with sand and mud unsuitable for exchange to supply the troops; he gave them Huai salt entirely, then reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Feng judged Longjiang salt, adulterated with sand and mud, unsuitable for exchange to supply the troops; he gave them Huai salt entirely and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉賞。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 又言留都重地，宜歲儲二百萬石，為根本計。

translations.literal: He also said that the secondary capital was a vital place and should store two million shi each year as a foundational reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the secondary capital was a vital place and should maintain an annual reserve of two million shi as a foundational safeguard.

sentences.zh: 從之，遂為令。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, and this became standing policy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and this became standing policy.

sentences.zh: 南京糧儲，舊督以都御史，十二年冬命鳳兼理。

translations.literal: Nanjing grain reserves had formerly been overseen by a censor-in-chief; in the winter of the twelfth year Feng was ordered to administer this concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing grain reserves had formerly been overseen by a censor-in-chief; in the winter of the twelfth year Feng was ordered to take charge of them concurrently.

sentences.zh: 廉謹善執法，號「板張」。

translations.literal: Incorruptible and conscientious and skilled in enforcing the law, he was called "Inflexible Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: Incorruptible, conscientious, and skilled in enforcing the law, he was known as "Inflexible Zhang."

sentences.zh: 景泰二年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingtai reign he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 四年改兵部，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書金濂卒，召鳳代之。

translations.literal: When Minister of Revenue Jin Lian died, Feng was summoned to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Jin Lian died, Feng was summoned to replace him.

sentences.zh: 時四方兵息，而災傷特甚。

translations.literal: At the time warfare had subsided throughout the realm, but disaster and crop failure were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: At the time warfare had subsided throughout the realm, but disasters and crop failures were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 帝屢詔寬恤。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts granting relief and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts granting relief and leniency.

sentences.zh: 鳳偕廷臣議上十事，明年復先後議上八事，鹹報可。

translations.literal: Feng together with court officials submitted ten proposals for deliberation; the next year eight more proposals were submitted in succession; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Feng together with court officials submitted ten proposals; the next year eight more were submitted in succession, and all were approved.

sentences.zh: 鳳以災傷蠲賦多，國用益詘，乃奏言：「國初天下田八百四十九萬餘頃，今數既減半，加以水旱停征，國用何以取給。

translations.literal: Feng, seeing that tax remissions due to disaster were numerous and state revenues increasingly strained, memorialized: "At the founding of the dynasty registered fields nationwide totaled more than 8.49 million qing; the figure has now been cut by half, and with drought and flood suspending collection, how is state revenue to be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: Feng, seeing that tax remissions due to disaster were numerous and state revenues increasingly strained, memorialized: "At the founding of the dynasty registered fields nationwide totaled more than 8.49 million qing; the figure has now been cut in half, and with drought and flood suspending collection, how is state revenue to be supplied?

sentences.zh: 京畿及河南、山東無額田，甲方墾辟，乙即訐其漏賦。

translations.literal: In the capital region and in Henan and Shandong there are unregistered fields: when one party clears and cultivates them, another immediately denounces them for evading tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital region and in Henan and Shandong there are unregistered fields: when one party clears and cultivates them, another immediately denounces them for evading tax.

sentences.zh: 請准輕則征租，不惟永絕爭端，亦且少助軍國。」

translations.literal: I ask permission to collect rent under a lighter standard—not only to end disputes permanently but also to provide some aid to army and state."
translations.idiomatic: I ask permission to collect rent under a lighter standard—not only to end disputes permanently but also to provide some aid to army and state."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 給事中成章等劾鳳擅更祖制，楊穟等復爭之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Cheng Zhang and others impeached Feng for changing ancestral institutions on his own authority; Yang Sui and others again disputed the policy.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Cheng Zhang and others impeached Feng for altering ancestral institutions on his own authority; Yang Sui and others again disputed the policy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國初都江南，轉輸易。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At the founding the capital was in the south and transport was easy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "At the founding the capital was in the south and transport was easy.

sentences.zh: 今居極北，可守常制耶？」

translations.literal: Now we sit at the far north—can we cling to the old standard?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we sit at the far north—can we cling to the old standard?"

sentences.zh: 四方報凶荒者，鳳請令御史勘實。

translations.literal: When reports of famine arrived from all quarters, Feng asked that censors be sent to verify them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When reports of famine arrived from all quarters, Feng asked that censors be sent to verify them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 議者非之。

translations.literal: Critics objected to this.
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected to this.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，調南京戶部，仍兼督糧儲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored his rule, Feng was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue at Nanjing and still concurrently supervised grain reserves.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong restored his rule, Feng was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue at Nanjing and continued to supervise grain reserves concurrently.

sentences.zh: 五年二月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second month of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the fifth year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 鳳有孝行。

translations.literal: Feng was filial in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was filial in conduct.

sentences.zh: 性淳樸。

translations.literal: His character was simple and honest.
translations.idiomatic: His character was simple and honest.

sentences.zh: 故人死，聘其女為子婦，教其子而養其母終身。

translations.literal: When an old friend died, he betrothed the friend's daughter to his son, educated his son, and supported the friend's mother for life.
translations.idiomatic: When an old friend died, he betrothed the friend's daughter to his son, educated his son, and supported the friend's mother for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 同學友蘇洪好面斥鳳過，及為鳳屬官猶然。

translations.literal: His schoolmate Su Hong liked to rebuke Feng's faults to his face; even after becoming one of Feng's subordinates he still did so.
translations.idiomatic: His schoolmate Su Hong liked to rebuke Feng's faults to his face; even after becoming one of Feng's subordinates he still did so.

sentences.zh: 鳳待之如初，聞其貧，即賙給之。

translations.literal: Feng treated him as before; hearing that he was poor, he immediately gave him relief.
translations.idiomatic: Feng treated him as before; hearing that he was poor, he immediately gave him relief.

sentences.zh: 周瑄，字廷玉，陽曲人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuan, styled Tingyu, was a native of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuan, styled Tingyu, was from Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉入國學。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination he entered the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: Through the provincial examination he entered the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 正統中，除刑部主事，善治獄。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was skilled at handling cases.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was skilled at handling cases.

sentences.zh: 十三年遷員外郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝北征。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor marched north on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor marched north on campaign.

sentences.zh: 郎中當扈從者多托疾，瑄請行。

translations.literal: Many directors who were to accompany the expedition feigned illness; Xuan volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Many directors who were to accompany the expedition feigned illness; Xuan volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 六師覆沒，瑄被創歸，擢署郎中。

translations.literal: When the army was destroyed, Xuan was wounded and returned; he was promoted to acting director.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was destroyed at Tumu, Xuan was wounded and returned; he was promoted to acting director.

sentences.zh: 校尉受賕縱盜，以仇人代。

translations.literal: A prison guard took a bribe and released a thief, substituting an enemy in his place.
translations.idiomatic: A prison guard took a bribe and released a thief, substituting an enemy in his place.

sentences.zh: 瑄辨雪之，抵校尉罪。

translations.literal: Xuan cleared the innocent man and punished the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan cleared the innocent man and punished the guard.

sentences.zh: 外郡送囚，一日至八百人。

translations.literal: Prisoners sent in from outlying prefectures reached eight hundred in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners sent in from outlying prefectures reached eight hundred in a single day.

sentences.zh: 瑄慮其觸熱，三日決遣之殆盡。

translations.literal: Xuan, fearing they would suffer in the heat, disposed of nearly all the cases within three days.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, fearing they would suffer in the heat, disposed of nearly all the cases within three days.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，以尚書王直薦，超拜刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, on the recommendation of Minister Wang Zhi, he was leapfrogged to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingtai reign, on the recommendation of Minister Wang Zhi, he was promoted directly to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 久之，出振順天、河間饑。

translations.literal: After some time he was sent out to relieve famine in Shuntian and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out to relieve famine in Shuntian and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 未竣，而英宗復位。

translations.literal: Before he had finished, Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished, Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne.

sentences.zh: 有司請召還。

translations.literal: The local offices requested that he be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The local offices requested that he be recalled.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not consent.

sentences.zh: 復賜敕，令便宜處置。

translations.literal: He was again granted an edict empowering him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He was again granted an edict empowering him to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 瑄遍曆所部，大舉荒政，先後振饑民二十六萬五千，給牛種各萬餘，奏行利民八事。

translations.literal: Xuan toured his jurisdiction thoroughly and launched major famine relief, succoring 265,000 starving people in all, distributing more than ten thousand head of cattle and seed grain each, and memorializing eight measures to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan toured his jurisdiction thoroughly and launched major famine relief, succoring 265,000 starving people in all, distributing more than ten thousand head of cattle and seed grain each, and memorializing eight measures to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 事竣還，明年轉左。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he returned; the next year he was transferred to the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he returned; the next year he was transferred to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 帝方任門達、逯杲，數興大獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Men Da and Lu Gao, and major prosecutions were repeatedly launched.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then relying on Men Da and Lu Gao, and major prosecutions were repeatedly launched.

sentences.zh: 瑄委曲開諭，多所救正，復飭諸郎毋避禍。

translations.literal: Xuan tactfully advised and persuaded, saving and correcting many cases, and also admonished the various directors not to shun danger.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan tactfully advised and persuaded, saving and correcting many cases, and also admonished the various directors not to shun danger.

sentences.zh: 以故移部定罪者，不至冤濫。

translations.literal: Thus those whose cases were transferred to the ministry for judgment did not suffer wrongful or excessive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, cases referred to the ministry for adjudication rarely resulted in unjust or excessive penalties.

sentences.zh: 官刑部久，屬吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Having served in the Ministry of Justice for a long time, subordinate officials did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the Ministry of Justice, his subordinates did not dare deceive him.

sentences.zh: 意主寬恕，不為深文。

translations.literal: His intent favored leniency; he did not apply harsh legal interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: He inclined toward clemency and refused to stretch the law for harsh convictions.

sentences.zh: 同佐部者安化孔文英，為御史時按黃岩妖言獄，當坐者三千人，皆白其誣，獨械首從一人論罪。

translations.literal: His colleague in the ministry, Kong Wenying of Anhua, when serving as censor had investigated the Huangyan sedition case; three thousand people were liable to punishment, but he cleared them all of false charges and put shackles only on the ringleader and one follower to fix guilt.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague at the ministry, Kong Wenying of Anhua, had previously investigated the Huangyan sedition case as a censor. Three thousand people faced conviction, but he exposed the charges as false and had only the ringleader and one accomplice shackled and sentenced.

sentences.zh: 及是居部，與瑄並稱長者。

translations.literal: When he now held office in the ministry, he and Xuan were both called elders of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Now serving together in the ministry, he and Xuan were alike hailed as men of stature and integrity.

sentences.zh: 七年命瑄署掌工部事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to administer the Ministry of Works affairs in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Xuan was appointed to handle the affairs of the Ministry of Works on an acting basis.

sentences.zh: 瑄恬靜淡榮利。

translations.literal: Xuan was tranquil and quiet, indifferent to glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was serene by nature and cared little for rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，為侍郎十六年矣，始遷右都御史。

translations.literal: When the Chenghua reign began its first year, he had already been a vice minister for sixteen years; only then was he promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the proclamation of the Chenghua era he had already served sixteen years as a vice minister before he was finally promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 督理南京糧儲，捕懲作奸者數輩，宿弊為清。

translations.literal: Supervising Nanjing grain stores, he seized and punished several fraudsters, and long-standing abuses were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: While overseeing Nanjing's grain reserves, he arrested and punished several ringleaders of corruption, clearing away entrenched abuses.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽、淮、徐饑，以瑄言發廩四十萬以振。

translations.literal: Famine struck Fengyang, Huai, and Xu; on Xuan's recommendation four hundred thousand [units of grain] were released from granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Fengyang, the Huai region, and Xu, the court followed Xuan's advice and opened the granaries to distribute four hundred thousand units of grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was appointed Minister of Justice in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 令諸司事不須勘者，毋出五日。

translations.literal: He ordered that matters among the offices that required no further investigation were not to exceed five days in processing.
translations.idiomatic: He required that any office matter not needing further review be settled within five days.

sentences.zh: 獄無滯囚。

translations.literal: The prisons held no detained prisoners overdue in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: No prisoners languished in his jails awaiting judgment.

sentences.zh: 暑疫，悉遣輕系者，曰：「召汝則至。」

translations.literal: During a summer epidemic, he released all lightly detained prisoners, saying, "When summoned, you must come."
translations.idiomatic: During a summer epidemic, he released all lightly detained prisoners, saying, "When I summon you, come at once."

sentences.zh: 囚歡呼去，無失期者。

translations.literal: The prisoners went off shouting for joy, and none failed to return on time.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners left cheering, and not one missed the appointed day of return.

sentences.zh: 為尚書九載，屢疏乞休。

translations.literal: Having served as minister for nine years, he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years as minister, he repeatedly petitioned for retirement.

sentences.zh: 久之乃得請。

translations.literal: Only after a long time was his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: Only after considerable time was his request granted.

sentences.zh: 家無田園，卜居南京。

translations.literal: His family owned no fields or gardens; he chose to dwell in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: With no fields or estate of his own, he settled in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，諡莊懿。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous name Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and honored with the posthumous title Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 長子經，尚書，自有傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jing became a minister and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jing rose to become a minister and has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 次子紘，進士，為南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: His second son Hong, a jinshi, served as a supervising secretary in the Nanjing directorate of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Hong, a jinshi, served as a supervising secretary in the Nanjing directorate of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 兩以災異言事。

translations.literal: Twice he spoke on state affairs citing calamities and omens.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he memorialized the throne, invoking omens and catastrophes as his occasion to speak.

sentences.zh: 帝並嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted both memorials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與御史張昺閱軍，為中官蔣琮誣奏，貶南京光祿署丞。

translations.literal: Before long, while inspecting troops with Censor Zhang Bing, he was falsely impeached by the eunuch Jiang Cong and demoted to assistant director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while inspecting troops with Censor Zhang Bing, he was falsely accused by the eunuch Jiang Cong and demoted to assistant director at the Nanjing Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 仕終山東參議。

translations.literal: He ended his career as an assistant provincial commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as assistant provincial commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 楊鼎，字宗器，陝西咸寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Ding, styled Zongqi, was a native of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding, styled Zongqi, was from Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 家貧力學，舉鄉會試第一。

translations.literal: Though his family was poor he studied hard, and came first in both the provincial and metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but diligent in his studies, he placed first in both the provincial and metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 正統四年，殿試第二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong he placed second in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengtong he ranked second in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 久之，與侍講杜寧等十人，簡入東閣肄業。

translations.literal: After some time, together with Expositor Du Ning and nine others, he was selected to study at the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was chosen, together with Expositor Du Ning and nine others, to pursue advanced study in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 鼎居侍從，雅欲以功名見。

translations.literal: Ding held a position close to the throne and naturally wished to make his mark through achievement and renown.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the imperial entourage, Ding aspired to distinguish himself in service and reputation.

sentences.zh: 嘗建言修飭戎備、通漕三邊二事。

translations.literal: He once proposed two measures: tightening military preparedness and opening grain transport to the three border regions.
translations.idiomatic: He once urged two reforms—strengthening border defenses and establishing grain transport to the three frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 同輩誚其迂，鼎益自信。

translations.literal: His peers mocked him as impractical, but Ding grew only more confident.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues ridiculed him as pedantic, yet Ding only grew more convinced of his course.

sentences.zh: 也先將寇京師，詔行監察御史事，募兵兗州。

translations.literal: When Esen was about to invade the capital region, an edict ordered him to act as investigating censor and raise troops at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Esen prepared to strike toward the capital, Ding was ordered to serve as an investigating censor and raise troops at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年進侍講兼中允。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai he was promoted to expositor and concurrently assistant tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai he was promoted to expositor and assistant tutor.

sentences.zh: 五年超擢戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was exceptionally promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received an exceptional promotion to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 天順初轉左。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was transferred to the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianshun reign he moved to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 陳汝言譖之。

translations.literal: Chen Ruyan slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruyan slandered him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to heed the accusation.

sentences.zh: 三年冬以陪祀陵寢不謹下獄，贖杖還職。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he was imprisoned for impropriety while attending sacrificial rites at the imperial tombs; after redeeming the cane punishment he returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he was jailed for a lapse in decorum during tomb rites; after paying a fine in lieu of corporal punishment he resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗命中官牛玉諭旨，欲取江南折糧銀實內帑，而以他稅物充武臣俸。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered the eunuch Niu Yu to convey his intent: to take the grain-conversion silver from Jiangnan to fill the inner treasury, and use other taxed goods to pay military officers' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once had the eunuch Niu Yu deliver an instruction to transfer Jiangnan's grain-conversion silver into the imperial privy purse and substitute other tax goods for stipends owed to military officers.

sentences.zh: 鼎不可。

translations.literal: Ding refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ding refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 馬牛芻乏，議征什二，又以民艱力沮。

translations.literal: Horses and cattle lacked fodder; a levy of one-fifth was proposed, but again he blocked it because of the people's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When fodder for horses and cattle ran short, officials proposed a twenty-percent levy, but Ding again blocked it out of concern for the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 皆報罷。

translations.literal: In every case the proposals were reported rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In every case the proposals were shelved at his instance.

sentences.zh: 七年，尚書年富有疾，詔鼎掌部事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Minister Nian Fu was aged and ill, an edict ordered Ding to manage ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, with Minister Nian Fu aged and infirm, the court ordered Ding to direct ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，代馬昂為戶部尚書，而以翁世資為侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua he replaced Ma Ang as Minister of Revenue, and Weng Shizi was made vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chenghua he succeeded Ma Ang as Minister of Revenue, with Weng Shizi appointed vice minister.

sentences.zh: 六年，鼎疏言：「陝西外患四寇，內患流民。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Ding memorialized: "Shaanxi suffers fourfold external trouble from raiders and internal trouble from displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Ding memorialized: "Shaanxi faces fourfold external threat from raiders and internal threat from displaced people.

sentences.zh: 然寇害止邊塞，流民則疾在腹心。

translations.literal: Yet the harm of raiders stops at the frontier, while displaced people afflict the very heart of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders harm only the frontier, but displaced people afflict the province at its core.

sentences.zh: 漢中僻居萬山，襟喉川蜀，四方流民數萬，急之生變，置之有後憂。

translations.literal: Hanzhong lies remote among myriad mountains, a strategic throat toward Sichuan; tens of thousands of migrants from all quarters have gathered there—push them hard and revolt may follow, leave them unchecked and trouble will come later.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong lies remote among countless mountains, guarding the approach to Sichuan; tens of thousands of migrants from every quarter have gathered there—drive them too hard and revolt may follow, leave them unchecked and trouble will come later.

sentences.zh: 請暫設監司一人，專領其事。

translations.literal: I ask that a regional commissioner be temporarily appointed to take charge of the matter exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a regional commissioner be temporarily appointed to take exclusive charge of the matter.

sentences.zh: 其願附籍者聽之，不願者資遣。

translations.literal: Let those who wish register locally; those who do not, supply them with funds and send them home.
translations.idiomatic: Let those who wish to register locally do so; those who do not, supply them with travel funds and send them home.

sentences.zh: 兼與守臣練士馬，修城池，庶可弭他日患。」

translations.literal: Together with the defending officials, drill troops and horses and repair walls and moats, so that future trouble may perhaps be averted."
translations.idiomatic: Together with local defenders, drill troops and horses and repair walls and moats, so that future trouble may be averted."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 湖廣頻歲饑，發廩已盡。

translations.literal: Huguang had suffered famine year after year, and granary distributions were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Huguang had gone hungry until its relief granaries were empty.

sentences.zh: 及是有秋，用鼎言，發庫貯銀布，易米備災。

translations.literal: When that year brought a harvest, on Ding's advice silver and cloth from treasury stores were released and exchanged for grain against future disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When a harvest finally came, the court followed Ding's advice and released stored silver and cloth from the treasury, exchanging them for grain to hold against future famine.

sentences.zh: 淮、徐、臨、德四倉，舊積糧百余萬石，後餉乏民饑，輒請移用，粟且匱。

translations.literal: The four granaries at Huai, Xu, Linqing, and Dezhou once held more than a million shi of grain in reserve; later, when supplies ran short and the people hungered, requests to shift the reserves were repeatedly granted, and the grain was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The four granaries at Huai, Xu, Linqing, and Dezhou once held more than a million shi in reserve, but as supplies tightened and famine spread, officials kept requisitioning the stores until little grain remained.

sentences.zh: 鼎議上贖罪、中鹽、折鈔、征逋六事行之。

translations.literal: Ding proposed six measures—redemption of crimes, salt vouchers, conversion to paper money, and collection of arrears among them—and had them enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Ding put forward six revenue measures—including fines in lieu of punishment, salt vouchers, conversion of obligations into paper notes, and collection of tax arrears—and had them implemented.

sentences.zh: 由是諸倉有儲蓄。

translations.literal: Thereby the various granaries came to have reserves again.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the granaries once again held reserves.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally granted the title Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 鼎居戶部，持廉，然性頗拘滯。

translations.literal: While at the Ministry of Revenue, Ding maintained integrity, yet his temperament was rather rigid and inflexible.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of revenue Ding remained incorruptible, yet his temperament was stiff and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 十五年秋，給事御史劾鼎非經國才。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifteenth year censors and supervising secretaries impeached Ding as lacking the talent to govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifteenth year supervising secretaries and censors impeached him as unfit for statecraft.

sentences.zh: 鼎再疏求去。

translations.literal: Ding again memorialized requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Ding again asked to be released from office.

sentences.zh: 賜敕馳驛歸，命有司月給米二石，歲給役四人，終其身。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial decree to return home by post relay; local officials were ordered to give him two shi of grain each month and four corvée servants each year for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him an edict to ride the post roads home and ordered local officials to supply two shi of grain monthly and four servants annually for life.

sentences.zh: 大臣致仕有給賜，自鼎始也。

translations.literal: Stipends and gifts upon retirement for great ministers began with Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of granting retired great ministers stipends and attendants began with Ding.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was posthumously granted Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous name Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 子時畼，進士，累官侍講學士。

translations.literal: His son Shi Chang, a jinshi, rose through the ranks to Hanlin expositor and academician.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Chang, a jinshi, rose to become an expositor and academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 多識典故，有用世才。

translations.literal: He knew many historical precedents and possessed talent useful to the age.
translations.idiomatic: Widely versed in precedent, he had genuine talent for public service.

sentences.zh: 時敷，舉人，廬墓被旌，官兵部司務。

translations.literal: Shi Fu, a provincial graduate, was honored for keeping vigil at his parents' tomb and served as a clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Fu, a provincial graduate, won imperial commendation for mourning at his parents' graveside and served as a clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 翁世資者，莆田人。

translations.literal: Weng Shizi was a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Shizi was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the seventh year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the seventh year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事，曆郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and served through to director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Revenue as a secretary and rose through the ranks to director.

sentences.zh: 天順元年拜工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun he was made Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 四年命中官往蘇、松、杭、嘉、湖增織彩幣七千匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor ordered eunuchs to Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou to increase woven brocade production by seven thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the court sent eunuchs to Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou to add seven thousand bolts to brocade production.

sentences.zh: 世資以東南水潦，民艱食，議減其半。

translations.literal: Shizi, citing flooding in the southeast and the people's difficulty in obtaining food, proposed halving the increase.
translations.idiomatic: With the southeast flooded and food scarce, Shizi proposed cutting the increase in half.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙榮、左侍郎霍瑄難之，世資請身任其咎，乃連署以諫。

translations.literal: Minister Zhao Rong and Left Vice Minister Huo Xuan objected; Shizi asked to bear the blame himself, and then jointly signed a remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhao Rong and Left Vice Minister Huo Xuan balked at the idea, but Shizi offered to accept personal responsibility and eventually joined them in a collective memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝果怒，詰主議者。

translations.literal: The emperor indeed grew angry and demanded who had initiated the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indeed furious and demanded to know who had led the opposition.

sentences.zh: 榮等委之世資，遂下詔獄，謫衡州知府。

translations.literal: Rong and the others shifted blame to Shizi, who was then sent to the imperial prison and demoted to prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and the others pinned the blame on Shizi, who was thrown into the imperial prison and demoted to prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化初，擢江西左布政使。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua he was promoted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he was promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 坐事下吏，尋得白。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned over an offense but soon cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He was briefly imprisoned on a charge but was soon cleared.

sentences.zh: 大軍征兩廣，轉江西餉，需十萬人。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned in the Two Guangs, transporting Jiangxi provisions required one hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When a major army marched against the Two Guangs, supplying its Jiangxi grain levy demanded one hundred thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 世資議齎直就易嶺南米。

translations.literal: Shizi proposed carrying cash south to purchase grain locally in Lingnan instead.
translations.idiomatic: Shizi proposed sending cash south to buy grain locally in Lingnan instead.

sentences.zh: 民得不擾。

translations.literal: The people were thus spared disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The people were spared the burden.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: As Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief he pacified and oversaw Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief he served as grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發倉儲五十余萬石以振，撫流亡百六十二萬人。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he released more than five hundred thousand shi from storehouses for relief and succored 1.62 million displaced persons.
translations.idiomatic: During famine he released more than five hundred thousand shi from storehouses for relief and succored 1.62 million refugees.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部右侍郎，佐鼎。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Revenue to assist Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Revenue to assist Ding.

sentences.zh: 久之，代薛遠總督倉場，進尚書。

translations.literal: After some time he replaced Xue Yuan as granary commissioner-general and was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In time he replaced Xue Yuan as granary commissioner-general and was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 十七年還理部事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned to manage ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he returned to direct ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 閱二年，致仕。

translations.literal: After two years he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he retired.

sentences.zh: 黃鎬，字叔高，侯官人。

translations.literal: Huang Gao, styled Shugao, was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gao, styled Shugao, was from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 正統十二年以進士試事都察院。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong, as a new jinshi he undertook probationary service at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong the new jinshi undertook probationary service at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 未半歲，以明習法律授御史。

translations.literal: In less than half a year, for his clear mastery of law he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he was appointed censor for his evident mastery of the law.

sentences.zh: 十四年按貴州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he toured and inspected Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he conducted an inspection tour of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 群苗盡叛，道梗塞。

translations.literal: The Miao tribes had all risen in revolt, and the roads were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao had risen everywhere, and the roads were cut off.

sentences.zh: 靖遠伯王驥等自麓川還，軍無紀律，苗襲其後，官軍大敗。

translations.literal: Marquis Jingyuan Wang Ji and others returning from Lucchuan had an undisciplined army; the Miao struck from behind and the government forces suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jingyuan Wang Ji and others, returning from Lucchuan with an undisciplined army, were struck from behind by the Miao and routed.

sentences.zh: 鎬赴平越，遇賊幾死。

translations.literal: Gao was heading to Pingyue when he met bandits and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was making for Pingyue when he ran into rebels and nearly lost his life.

sentences.zh: 夜跳入城，賊圍之。

translations.literal: By night he leaped into the city, and the bandits besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: He stole into the city by night, and the rebels laid siege.

sentences.zh: 議者欲棄城走，鎬曰：「平越，貴州咽喉，無平越是無貴州也。」

translations.literal: Some counseled abandoning the city and fleeing. Gao said: "Pingyue is the throat of Guizhou; without Pingyue there is no Guizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged abandoning the city and fleeing. Gao said: "Pingyue is the throat of Guizhou; without Pingyue there is no Guizhou."

sentences.zh: 乃偕諸將固守。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with the generals he held fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: He and the generals then resolved to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 置密疏竹筒中，募土人間行乞援於朝，且劾驥等覆師狀。

translations.literal: He placed a secret memorial in a bamboo tube, hired locals to travel by secret paths to beg aid from court, and also impeached Wang Ji and others for the disaster that destroyed the army.
translations.idiomatic: He hid a secret memorial in a bamboo tube, hired local men to slip through the lines and plead for relief at court, and also impeached Ji and others for the army's destruction.

sentences.zh: 景帝命保定伯梁珤等合川、湖軍救之，圍始解。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing ordered Marquis Baoding Liang Yu and others to combine Sichuan and Huguang forces to rescue them, and only then was the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing ordered Marquis Baoding Liang Yu to lead combined Sichuan and Huguang forces to their relief, and the siege was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 城被困已九月，掘草根煮弩鎧而食之，死者相枕籍。

translations.literal: The city had been besieged for nine months; they dug up grass roots and boiled crossbow gear to eat, and the dead lay piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: The siege had lasted nine months. Defenders dug up grass roots and boiled crossbow quivers for food; the dead lay stacked in heaps.

sentences.zh: 城卒全，鎬功為多。

translations.literal: The city was preserved in the end; Gao's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: The city was saved in the end, and Gao's contribution was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 復留按一年。

translations.literal: He remained another year to conduct inspections.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed on for another year of inspection duty.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷廣東僉事，改浙江。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to assistant commissioner in Guangdong, then reassigned to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was appointed assistant commissioner in Guangdong, then transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 成化初，以大臣會薦，擢廣東左參政。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua, on collective recommendation by great ministers, he was promoted to Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, recommended by senior ministers, he was promoted to left assistant administration commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 高、雷、廉負海多盜，鎬討平之。

translations.literal: Gaozhou, Leizhou, and Lianzhou bordered the sea and had many bandits; Gao suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhou, Leizhou, and Lianzhou lay on the coast and swarmed with pirates; Gao suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 再遷廣西左布政使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again, becoming left provincial administration commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史總督南京糧儲，曆吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: As Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief he served as superintendent of Nanjing grain reserves, and passed through Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief he superintended Nanjing's grain reserves, then served as left and right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十六年拜南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 鎬有才識，敏吏事，理鹽政，多所厘剔，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Gao had talent and insight; he was quick in administrative affairs, and in managing the salt administration he rectified many abuses; contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was capable and astute, quick with administrative affairs; in reforming the salt administration he cleared away many abuses, and contemporaries spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 十九年致仕，道卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he retired, and died on the road home.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he retired and died on the journey home.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，諡襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous name Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 胡拱辰，字共之，淳安人。

translations.literal: Hu Gongchen, styled Gongzhi, was a native of Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Gongchen, styled Gongzhi, was from Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 正統四年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 為黟縣知縣，有惠政，擢御史。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Yi County he had benevolent policies and was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Yi County he won the people's goodwill and was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 疏陳時弊八事。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth eight current abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne with eight pressing abuses of the age.

sentences.zh: 父艱歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he returned home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，詔科道官憂居者悉起復。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, an edict ordered all censorial and supervisory officials in mourning to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he ordered every censor and supervising secretary in mourning to return to office.

sentences.zh: 拱辰至，屢疏以選將、保邦、修德、弭災為言，出為貴州左參政。

translations.literal: When Gongchen arrived he repeatedly memorialized on selecting generals, safeguarding the realm, cultivating virtue, and averting calamities; he was sent out as Left Assistant Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once back at court, Gongchen repeatedly memorialized on choosing generals, securing the realm, cultivating virtue, and averting disaster—then was posted out as left assistant commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 白水堡仡佬頭目沈時保素梗化，拱辰言于總兵官方瑛遣將擒之。

translations.literal: Shen Shibao, a Gelao chieftain at Baishuibao, had long resisted assimilation; Gongchen told Regional Commander Fang Ying to send officers to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shibao, a Gelao chieftain at Baishuibao, had long resisted assimilation; Gongchen urged Regional Commander Fang Ying to send troops to capture him.

sentences.zh: 一方遂寧。

translations.literal: The region was then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: That region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 至畢節，平宣慰使隴富亂，威行邊徼。

translations.literal: When he reached Bijie, he put down the rebellion of Pacification Commissioner Long Fu, and his authority extended along the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At Bijie he put down the rebellion of pacification commissioner Long Fu, and his authority reached every corner of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 母憂去，御史追劾其受賕事，下浙江按臣執訊。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning; a censor pursued charges of bribery against him, and he was handed to the touring inspector of Zhejiang for examination.
translations.idiomatic: When he left to mourn his mother, a censor pursued bribery charges against him and had him interrogated by the touring inspector of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 事白，調廣東。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared, he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Cleared of wrongdoing, he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 曆廣西、四川左、右布政使，皆有平寇功。

translations.literal: He served as left and right provincial administration commissioner in Guangxi and Sichuan, and in each place had merit in pacifying bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right provincial administration commissioner in Guangxi and Sichuan, earning merit for pacifying bandits in each post.

sentences.zh: 成化八年拜南京右副都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing and put in charge of training and defense along the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chenghua he became Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing with charge of riverine training and defense.

sentences.zh: 十一年就遷兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promptly promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was immediately promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 儲位虛久，與尚書崔恭等請冊立，言甚切。

translations.literal: The heir apparent's place had long stood empty; together with Minister Cui Gong and others he petitioned to establish a crown prince, speaking with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's place had long been vacant; he joined Minister Cui Gong and others in urgently petitioning to install a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 其年復就改左副都御史總理糧儲，就進工部尚書。

translations.literal: That same year he was promptly transferred to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief to superintend grain supplies, and was immediately promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he moved at once to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief overseeing grain reserves, then was immediately promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 節財省事，人皆便之。

translations.literal: He economized finances and streamlined affairs, and all found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He cut costs and streamlined procedures, to everyone's relief.

sentences.zh: 以年至乞歸。

translations.literal: On account of age he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his age, he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，巡按御史陳銓言：「拱辰退休十餘年，生平清操如一日，乞加禮異以勵臣節。」

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, Touring Inspector Chen Quan said: "Gongchen has been retired more than ten years, and his lifelong integrity remains unchanged; I beg that special honors be granted to encourage ministerial constancy."
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, Touring Inspector Chen Quan said: "Gongchen has been retired more than ten years, and his lifelong integrity remains as steadfast as ever; I beg that special honors be granted to encourage ministerial constancy."

sentences.zh: 詔有司月給廩二石，歲隸四人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the local offices to grant him two shi of grain stipend each month and four household retainers each year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered local offices to grant him two shi of grain stipend each month and four household retainers each year.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，年九十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was ninety years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he was ninety years old.

sentences.zh: 遣行人齎敕存問，賚羊酒，加賜廩、隸。

translations.literal: An emissary was dispatched bearing an imperial letter to inquire after his health, bestowing sheep and wine and granting additional grain stipends and retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an emissary bearing an imperial letter to inquire after his health, with gifts of sheep and wine and additional grain stipends and retainers.

sentences.zh: 三年正月卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅，諡莊懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 陳俊，字時英，莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Jun, styled Shiying, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jun, styled Shiying, was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: He placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He came first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Revenue as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 督天津諸衛軍采草，奏減新增額三十五萬束。

translations.literal: Supervising the military guards of Tianjin in gathering fodder grass, he memorialized to reduce the new additional quota by three hundred fifty thousand bundles.
translations.idiomatic: While overseeing fodder collection by the Tianjin garrisons, he memorialized to cut the newly imposed quota by three hundred fifty thousand bundles.

sentences.zh: 豪猾侵蘇、松改折銀七十余萬兩，俊往督，不數月畢輸。

translations.literal: Powerful schemers had embezzled more than seven hundred thousand taels of grain-conversion silver from Suzhou and Songjiang; Jun went to supervise, and within a few months all was paid in full.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful schemers had embezzled more than seven hundred thousand taels of Suzhou and Songjiang grain-conversion silver; Jun went to collect it, and within months the full sum was recovered.

sentences.zh: 尚書金濂以為能，俾典諸曹章奏。

translations.literal: Minister Jin Lian judged him capable and had him manage memorials among the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Lian, impressed by his ability, put him in charge of memorials for the ministry's bureaus.

sentences.zh: 曆郎中。

translations.literal: He served through to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director.

sentences.zh: 天順五年，兩廣用兵，俊督餉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun, when the Two Guangs were at war, Jun supervised supplies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianshun, with the Two Guangs at war, Jun directed supply lines.

sentences.zh: 時州縣殘破，帑藏殫虛，弛鹽商越境令，引加米二斗，軍興賴以無乏。

translations.literal: At the time prefectures and counties lay in ruins, treasuries were exhausted; he relaxed the prohibition on salt merchants crossing borders and added two dou of grain per cartload, and through this the army's needs were met without shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: With prefectures in ruins and treasuries empty, he relaxed the ban on salt merchants crossing borders and added two dou of grain per shipment—enough to keep the armies supplied.

sentences.zh: 母喪，不聽歸，蠻平始還。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was not permitted to return; only after the barbarians were pacified did he come back.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death went unheeded—the court refused his leave until the rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 初，俊為主事，奔父喪，賻者皆卻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jun was a secretary and rushed home for his father's funeral, he refused all condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as a secretary rushing home for his father's funeral, he refused every condolence gift.

sentences.zh: 至是文武將吏醵金賻，亦不納。

translations.literal: Now civil and military officers pooled money as condolence gifts, but he likewise refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Now civil and military officers pooled cash as a condolence gift, and he refused that too.

sentences.zh: 成化初，擢南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua he was promoted to Vice Director of Ceremonies at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he was promoted to Vice Director of Ceremonies at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 四年召拜戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled to court as Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 俊練習錢穀。

translations.literal: Jun was well versed in revenue and grain accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was thoroughly versed in fiscal administration.

sentences.zh: 四方災傷，邊鎮急芻餉。

translations.literal: Calamities and crop failures struck all quarters, and frontier garrisons urgently needed fodder and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster struck every quarter, and frontier garrisons urgently needed fodder and supplies.

sentences.zh: 奏請遝至，裁決咸當，尚書楊鼎深倚之。

translations.literal: Memorials requesting decisions arrived one after another; his rulings were all apt; Minister Yang Ding relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials poured in for his decision; his rulings were unfailingly sound, and Minister Yang Ding relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 京師大饑，先後發太倉粟八十萬石平糴。

translations.literal: Great famine struck the capital; in two phases eight hundred thousand shi of grain from the Great Granary were released for sale at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the capital, the court twice released eight hundred thousand shi from the Great Granary for sale at controlled prices.

sentences.zh: 石值六錢，豪猾乘時射利。

translations.literal: Each shi was priced at six qian; powerful schemers seized the moment to reap profits.
translations.idiomatic: At six qian per shi, the powerful seized the moment to profiteer.

sentences.zh: 俊請糴以升鬥為率，過一石勿與。

translations.literal: Jun requested that grain be sold by sheng and dou as the measure, and that no buyer receive more than one shi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun proposed selling grain by the cup and peck, with no buyer allowed more than one shi.

sentences.zh: 饑民獲濟。

translations.literal: Starving people obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: The hungry were fed.

sentences.zh: 尋議用兵河套，敕俊赴河南、山、陝，會巡撫諸臣畫芻餉，發帑金二十萬助之。

translations.literal: Soon there was discussion of campaigning in the Ordos; an edict ordered Jun to Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi to meet with the grand coordinators and plan fodder and supplies, and two hundred thousand taels from the treasury were released to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated an Ordos campaign, Jun was dispatched to Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi to confer with grand coordinators on supply plans, with two hundred thousand taels from the treasury to assist.

sentences.zh: 俊以邊庾空竭，歲又不登，而榆林道險遠，轉輸難，乃發金于內地市易。

translations.literal: Jun, noting that frontier granaries were empty, the year's harvest failed, and the route to Yulin was rugged and distant making transport difficult, released funds to purchase grain in interior markets.
translations.idiomatic: With frontier granaries empty, the harvest poor, and the road to Yulin long and perilous, Jun released funds to buy grain in interior markets instead.

sentences.zh: 修西安、韓城、同官徑道，以利飛輓。

translations.literal: He repaired direct routes through Xi'an, Hancheng, and Tongguan to facilitate rapid transport.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired direct routes through Xi'an, Hancheng, and Tongguan to speed transport.

sentences.zh: 還朝，進俸一級，曆吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he received one step advancement in salary rank and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he received a salary increase and served as left and right vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 九載滿，拜南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When nine years were completed, he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years' service he was appointed Minister of Revenue in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Ministry of War to assist in matters of state.

sentences.zh: 先是，參贊之任，不專屬兵部，自薛遠後，繼以俊，遂為定制。

translations.literal: Previously the post of assistant in state affairs did not belong exclusively to the Ministry of War; since Xue Yuan, Jun followed, and it became fixed custom.
translations.idiomatic: Until then the post of assisting in state affairs had not belonged exclusively to the Ministry of War; after Xue Yuan came Jun, and the arrangement became permanent custom.

sentences.zh: 久之，就改吏部。

translations.literal: After some time he was promptly transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，星變，率九卿陳時弊二十事，皆極痛切。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, on an alteration of the stars, he led the Nine Ministers in setting forth twenty current abuses, all spoken with utmost severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, when the heavens shifted, he led the Nine Ministers in memorializing twenty abuses of the age—each framed with brutal candor.

sentences.zh: 帝多採納。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted much of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted many of their recommendations.

sentences.zh: 而權幸所不便者，終格不行。

translations.literal: Yet what was inconvenient to powerful favorites was ultimately blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But measures that discomfited powerful favorites were ultimately blocked.

sentences.zh: 明年乞致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子少保，賜敕馳傳還。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and granted an imperial decree to return home by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him the title Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and an edict to ride the post roads home.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡康懿。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was given the posthumous name Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous title Kangyi.

sentences.zh: 林鶚，字一鶚，浙江太平人。

translations.literal: Lin E, styled Yie, was a native of Taiping in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin E, styled Yie, was from Taiping in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the second year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 授御史，監京畿鄉試。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor and supervised the metropolitan circuit's provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor and supervised the provincial examination for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 陳循等訐考官，鶚邑子林挺預薦，疑鶚有私，逮挺考訊。

translations.literal: Chen Xun and others denounced the examiners; Lin E's fellow-townsman Lin Ting had been recommended, and suspecting favoritism they arrested Ting for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun and others challenged the examiners. Lin E's townsman Lin Ting had been recommended, and suspecting favoritism they arrested Ting for questioning.

sentences.zh: 挺實無他，得白。

translations.literal: Ting truly had no irregularity and was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was found blameless and cleared.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，仿先朝故事，出廷臣為知府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, following the precedent of earlier reigns he sent court officials out as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, the court revived the old practice of sending senior officials out as prefects.

sentences.zh: 鶚得鎮江。

translations.literal: Lin E was assigned Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin E was assigned to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 召見，賜膳及道里費，諭所以擢用意。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience, granted a meal and travel expenses, and instructed of the emperor's intent in promoting him.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience, given a feast and travel funds, and told why the emperor had elevated him.

sentences.zh: 鶚感激，革弊舉廢，治甚有聲。

translations.literal: Lin E, deeply moved, abolished abuses and revived neglected projects; his governance gained great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the trust placed in him, Lin E rooted out abuses and revived neglected works; his governance won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 漕故經孟瀆，險甚。

translations.literal: The grain transport route formerly passed through Mengdu and was extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The grain transport route had run through Mengdu—a passage notoriously treacherous.

sentences.zh: 巡撫崔恭議鑿河，自七里港引金山上流通丹陽避之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Cui Gong proposed digging a canal from Qili Harbor to draw water from Jinshan upward and connect through Danyang to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Cui Gong proposed digging a canal from Qili Harbor, channeling water from Jinshan up through Danyang to bypass the danger.

sentences.zh: 鶚言：「道里遠，多石，且壞民廬墓。

translations.literal: Lin E said: "The route is long, there is much rock, and moreover it would ruin people's houses and graves.
translations.idiomatic: Lin E objected: "The route is too long and stony, and it would destroy homes and graves.

sentences.zh: 請按京口閘、甘露壩故跡，浚之令通舟。

translations.literal: I ask that we follow the old sites of the Jingkou sluice and Ganlu dam, dredge them, and make them passable for boats.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old Jingkou sluice and Ganlu dam sites instead—dredge them so boats can pass.

sentences.zh: 春夏啟閘，秋冬度壩，功力省便。」

translations.literal: In spring and summer open the sluice; in autumn and winter cross the dam—labor is saved and it is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Open the sluice in spring and summer, cross the dam in autumn and winter—far less labor, far more practical."

sentences.zh: 恭從其議，遂為永利。

translations.literal: Cui Gong followed his proposal, and it became a lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong adopted his plan, and the improvement endured.

sentences.zh: 居五年，以才任治劇，調蘇州。

translations.literal: After five years, on account of his talent for governing demanding posts, he was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After five years, recognized for his talent in governing difficult posts, he was transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化初，超遷江西按察使。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua he was exceptionally promoted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he was promoted ahead of schedule to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 有犯大辟賄達官求生者，鶚執愈堅。

translations.literal: When someone guilty of a capital crime bribed high officials to beg for his life, Lin E held firm all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When a man facing execution bribed officials for clemency, Lin E held all the more firmly to the law.

sentences.zh: 廣東寇剽贛州急。

translations.literal: Bandits from Guangdong raided Ganzhou urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong bandits were raiding Ganzhou with fierce urgency.

sentences.zh: 調兵禦之，遁去。

translations.literal: He mobilized troops to resist them, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched troops to repel them, and they fled.

sentences.zh: 廣信妖賊妄稱天神惑眾，捕戮其魁，立解散。

translations.literal: Sorcerer-rebels at Guangxin falsely claimed to be celestial gods to mislead the people; he captured and executed their ringleader, and they immediately dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Sorcerer-rebels at Guangxin were claiming divine status to mislead the people; he captured and executed their leader, and the mob scattered at once.

sentences.zh: 曆左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served as left and right provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奏減民租十五萬石。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he memorialized to reduce the people's land tax by one hundred fifty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: During famine he memorialized to cut land tax by one hundred fifty thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 成化六年，擢南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chenghua he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chenghua he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 母憂服除，召為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother was complete he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 執法不撓。

translations.literal: In administering the law he was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: In enforcing the law he never bent.

sentences.zh: 十二年得疾卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 鶚事母孝謹，對妻子無惰容。

translations.literal: Lin E served his mother with filial care, and showed no slackness before wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Lin E was filial and devoted to his mother, and never relaxed his decorum before wife or children.

sentences.zh: 不妄交與，公餘輒危坐讀書。

translations.literal: He did not casually associate with others; in spare hours from public duties he always sat upright reading.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his company carefully chosen, and in every spare hour sat upright with a book.

sentences.zh: 歿不能具棺斂，友人為經紀其喪。

translations.literal: At death he could not afford a proper coffin and burial; friends arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he could not afford a coffin; friends saw to his funeral.

sentences.zh: 鶚在蘇州，先聖像剝落。

translations.literal: When Lin E was in Suzhou, the sage's image had flaked and peeled.
translations.idiomatic: During Lin E's time in Suzhou, the sage's image had grown worn and flaking.

sentences.zh: 鶚曰：「塑像，非古也，昔太祖于國學用木主。」

translations.literal: Lin E said: "Statue images are not ancient custom; formerly Taizu used wooden tablets at the State Academy."
translations.idiomatic: Lin E said: "Statues are not ancient practice. Taizu himself used wooden spirit tablets at the State Academy."

sentences.zh: 命改從之。

translations.literal: He ordered a change to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the change carried out.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，御史趙大佑上其節行，贈刑部尚書，諡恭肅。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing era, Censor Zhao Dayou memorialized about his integrity and conduct; he was posthumously granted Minister of Justice and given the posthumous epithet Gongsu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, Censor Zhao Dayou submitted a memorial praising Lin E's integrity and conduct; the court posthumously granted him the title of Minister of Justice and the posthumous epithet Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 潘榮，字尊用，龍溪人。

translations.literal: Pan Rong, styled Zunyong, was a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Rong, styled Zunyong, was from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 犒師廣東，還，除吏科給事中。

translations.literal: After rewarding the troops in Guangdong, upon his return he was appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Branch.
translations.idiomatic: After distributing rewards to the troops in Guangdong, he returned and was appointed supervising secretary of the Personnel Branch.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，疏論停起復、抑奔競數事。

translations.literal: Early in Jingtai, he submitted a memorial discussing several matters: halting early reinstatement from mourning leave and curbing competitive scrambling for office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign, he submitted a memorial on several reforms, including ending premature recall from mourning leave and restraining the scramble for advancement.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 尋進右給事中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 四年九月上言：「致治之要，莫切於納諫。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year he memorialized: "The essential point in achieving good governance is nothing more urgent than accepting remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year he memorialized: "The key to good governance is nothing more urgent than heeding remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 比以言者忤聖意，諭禮部，凡遇建言，務加審察。

translations.literal: Recently, because remonstrators have offended the imperial will, an edict was issued to the Ministry of Rites that whenever advice is offered, it must be carefully scrutinized.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, because those who speak out have offended the throne, the Ministry of Rites has been instructed to scrutinize every memorial offering advice.

sentences.zh: 或假以報復，具奏罪之。

translations.literal: Sometimes on pretext of retaliation, full memorials are submitted to convict them.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes officials use the pretext of personal vendetta to submit full memorials calling for their punishment.

sentences.zh: 此令一下，廷臣喪氣，以言為諱。

translations.literal: Once this order was issued, court officials lost their spirit and came to treat speech as taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Once that order went out, court officials lost heart and fell silent, treating speech as something to be avoided.

sentences.zh: 國家有利害，生民有得失，大臣有奸慝，何由而知？

translations.literal: When the state has benefit or harm, the people have gain or loss, and great ministers harbor wickedness — how is one to know?
translations.idiomatic: How is the throne to learn when the state faces benefit or harm, when the people suffer gain or loss, or when high ministers conceal wicked designs?

sentences.zh: 況今巨寇陸梁，塞上多事，奈何反塞言者路。

translations.literal: Moreover, great bandits now run rampant and the frontier is beset with troubles — why, then, block the path of those who would speak?
translations.idiomatic: Great rebels now run rampant, and the frontier is in turmoil — why, then, cut off the path of those who would speak out?

sentences.zh: 望明詔台諫，知無不言，緘默者罪。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will clearly decree to the censorate and remonstrance officials that they must speak of whatever they know, and that silence shall be a crime.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a clear decree to the censorate and remonstrance officials: speak of whatever you know, and let silence be punished.

sentences.zh: 並敕閣部大臣，勿搜求參駁，虧傷治體。」

translations.literal: Also command the grand secretaries and ministry chiefs not to search out grounds for impeachment and refutation that damage the structure of governance."
translations.idiomatic: Also command the grand secretaries and ministry chiefs to stop hunting for grounds to impeach and refute remonstrance, which undermines the foundations of good government."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived at court, the emperor merely acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 天順六年使琉球，還，遷都給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianshun he served as envoy to Ryukyu; on his return he was transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianshun he went as envoy to Ryukyu, and on his return was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 成化六年三月偕同官上言：「近雨雪愆期，災異迭見。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Chenghua, together with fellow officials he memorialized: "Recently snow and rain have been out of season, and portents have appeared in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year of Chenghua, he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Snow and rain have lately fallen out of season, and ominous signs have appeared one after another.

sentences.zh: 陛下降詔自責，躬行祈禱，詔大臣盡言，宜上天感格。

translations.literal: Your Majesty issued an edict of self-reproach, personally performed prayers, and commanded the great ministers to speak fully — Heaven ought to have been moved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty issued an edict of self-reproach, prayed in person, and commanded your ministers to speak freely — Heaven ought surely to have been moved.

sentences.zh: 而今乃風霾晝晦，沴氣赤而復黑，豈非應天之道有未盡歟？

translations.literal: Yet now wind haze darkens the day at noon, and baleful vapors turn from red to black — is this not because the way of responding to Heaven has not been fully carried out?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now wind-borne haze darkens the sky at midday, and baleful vapors shift from red to black — is this not a sign that the way of responding to Heaven has not yet been fully honored?

sentences.zh: 夫人君敬天，不在齋戒祈禱而已。

translations.literal: For a ruler, reverence for Heaven is not limited to fasting and prayer alone.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's reverence for Heaven is not fulfilled by fasting and prayer alone.

sentences.zh: 政令乖宜，下民失所；

translations.literal: When government orders are ill-suited, the common people lose their livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: When government orders are ill-conceived, the common people lose their footing;

sentences.zh: 崇尚珍玩，費用不經；

translations.literal: when rare curios are prized and expenditures lack regulation;
translations.idiomatic: when rare treasures are prized and spending runs without restraint;

sentences.zh: 後宮無序，恩澤不均；

translations.literal: when the inner palace is without order and favor is unevenly distributed;
translations.idiomatic: when the inner palace falls into disorder and imperial favor is unevenly bestowed;

sentences.zh: 爵濫施於賤工，賞妄及於非分，皆非敬天之道。

translations.literal: when titles are lavishly given to base craftsmen and rewards rashly granted beyond what is fitting — none of these is the way of revering Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: when titles are lavished on lowly artisans and rewards recklessly granted beyond what is due — none of this is the way to revere Heaven.

sentences.zh: 願陛下日禦便殿，召大臣極陳缺失而厘革之，庶災變可弭。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will daily hold court in the side hall, summon the great ministers to set forth fully what is wanting and rectify it — then perhaps calamities and prodigies may be stilled."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to hold daily audience in the side hall, summon the great ministers to lay bare every failing and reform it — then perhaps these calamities may be stilled."

sentences.zh: 時萬妃專寵，群小夤緣進寶玩，官賞冗濫，故榮等懇言之。

translations.literal: At the time the Lady Wan enjoyed exclusive favor; lesser men climbed up to present treasures and curios, and official rewards were redundantly lavish — hence Rong and the others spoke earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lady Wan held exclusive favor; sycophants climbed up through her patronage to present treasures and curios, and official rewards flowed with wasteful abundance — hence Rong and his colleagues spoke so earnestly.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not act on their advice.

sentences.zh: 是年遷南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 又七年，就擢戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Seven years later he was directly promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later he was promoted directly to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋改右副都御史、總督南京糧儲。
