translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and Grand Coordinator of Nanjing grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and Grand Coordinator of Nanjing grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 積奇羨數萬石以備荒。

translations.literal: He accumulated surplus grain of tens of thousands of shi as a reserve against famine.
translations.idiomatic: He built up a surplus of tens of thousands of shi of grain as a reserve against famine.

sentences.zh: 十七年召為戶部左侍郎，尋署部事。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Revenue, and soon acted as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chenghua he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of Revenue and soon took charge of the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 英國公張懋等四十三人自陳先世以大功錫爵，子孫承繼，所司輒減歲祿，非祖宗報功意。

translations.literal: The Earl of Yingguo, Zhang Mao, and forty-three others stated that their forebears had been granted noble rank for great merit and that their descendants had inherited it, yet the responsible offices repeatedly reduced their annual stipends — contrary to the ancestral intent to reward merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Yingguo, Zhang Mao, and forty-three others petitioned that their forebears had been ennobled for great merit and that their descendants had inherited those titles, yet the responsible offices kept reducing their annual stipends — contrary to the ancestral intent to reward service.

sentences.zh: 榮等言：「懋等於無事時妄請增祿，若有功何以勸賞？

translations.literal: Rong and the others said: "Mao and the others recklessly petition for increased stipends in times of peace — if merit is thus rewarded, how can merit be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Rong and his colleagues objected: "Mao and the others are recklessly seeking increased stipends in a time of peace — if rewards are granted without merit, how can merit ever be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 況頻年水旱，國用未充，所請不可許。」

translations.literal: Moreover, with floods and droughts in successive years and state revenues not yet full, what they request cannot be granted."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with floods and droughts in successive years and the treasury still strained, their request cannot be granted."

sentences.zh: 事乃寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was dropped.

sentences.zh: 中官趙陽等乞兩淮鹽十萬引，帝已許之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhao Yang and others requested one hundred thousand salt certificates from the two Huai regions; the emperor had already granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhao Yang and others requested one hundred thousand salt certificates from the two Huai salt districts, and the emperor had already approved the grant.

sentences.zh: 榮等言：「近禁勢家中鹽，詔旨甫頒，而陽等輒違犯，宜正其罪。」

translations.literal: Rong and the others said: "Recently powerful families were forbidden from hoarding salt — the edict was just promulgated, yet Yang and the others immediately violated it; their crime should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Rong and his colleagues protested: "Powerful families were just forbidden to hoard salt — the edict has barely been issued, yet Yang and the others have already violated it. Their offense should be punished."

sentences.zh: 帝為切責陽等。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked Yang and the others on their account.
translations.idiomatic: On their account the emperor sharply rebuked Yang and his associates.

sentences.zh: 南京戶部尚書黃鎬罷，以榮代之。

translations.literal: Huang Gao, Minister of Revenue in Nanjing, was dismissed, and Rong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Gao was dismissed as Minister of Revenue in Nanjing, Rong was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，謝政歸。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he resigned from office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, Rong resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 賜月廩、歲夫如制。

translations.literal: He was granted monthly rations and annual corvée laborers according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted monthly stipends and annual corvée servants according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Hongzhi, at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 夏時正，字季爵，仁和人。

translations.literal: Xia Shizheng, styled Jijue, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shizheng, styled Jijue, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 正統十年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the tenth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年以郎中錄囚福建，出死罪六十餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai, as a bureau director he reviewed prisoners in Fujian and released more than sixty men under sentence of death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jingtai, serving as a bureau director on a prisoner-review tour in Fujian, he released more than sixty men under sentence of death.

sentences.zh: 中有減死、詔充所在濱海衛軍者，時正慮其入海島為變，轉發之山東，然後以聞。

translations.literal: Among them were some whose death sentences had been commuted and who by edict were to serve in coastal guard units of their locale; Shizheng feared they would flee to sea islands and make trouble, so he redirected them to Shandong before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were men whose death sentences had been commuted and who by edict were to serve in coastal guard units near their homes. Shizheng feared they might flee to offshore islands and stir up trouble, so he transferred them to Shandong before reporting what he had done.

sentences.zh: 因言：「凡福建減死囚，俱宜戍之北方。」

translations.literal: He therefore said: "All prisoners in Fujian whose death sentences have been commuted should be exiled to garrison duty in the north."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore argued: "All prisoners in Fujian whose death sentences have been commuted should be sent to garrison duty in the north."

sentences.zh: 法司是其言，而請治違詔罪。

translations.literal: The judicial offices agreed with his view but requested that he be punished for violating the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices agreed with his reasoning but asked that he be punished for disobeying the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝特宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 時正又言：「通番及劫盜諸獄，以待會讞。

translations.literal: Shizheng also said: "Cases of illegal foreign trade and robbery await joint review.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng also argued: "Cases of illegal foreign trade and robbery are left pending joint review.

sentences.zh: 淹引時月，囚多瘐死。

translations.literal: They drag on for months, and many prisoners die of illness in custody.
translations.idiomatic: They drag on for months, and many prisoners die of illness while waiting.

sentences.zh: 請令所司斷決。」

translations.literal: Please order the responsible offices to render judgment."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the responsible offices be ordered to decide these cases promptly."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，且推行之天下。

translations.literal: An edict approved this and extended it throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal and extended the practice throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 天順初，擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianshun reign he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 久之，以便養，遷南京大理少卿。

translations.literal: After a long time, citing convenience in caring for his parents, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After some years, citing the need to care for his parents, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 成化五年遷本寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua he was transferred to director of that court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chenghua he was transferred to director of the Court of Judicial Review in the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年春命巡視江西災傷。

translations.literal: The next spring he was ordered to inspect disaster damage in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was ordered to inspect disaster damage in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 除無名稅十余萬石，汰諸司冗役數萬，奏罷不職吏二百餘人，增築南昌濱江堤及豐城諸縣陂岸，民賴其利。

translations.literal: He abolished unnamed taxes totaling more than one hundred thousand shi, eliminated redundant corvée numbering in the tens of thousands across various offices, memorialized for the dismissal of more than two hundred incompetent officials, and reinforced the river embankment at Nanchang and the dykes and shores of various counties in Fengcheng — the people benefited from his work.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished unauthorized levies totaling more than one hundred thousand shi of grain, cut redundant corvée labor numbering in the tens of thousands across various offices, memorialized for the dismissal of more than two hundred incompetent officials, and reinforced the river embankment at Nanchang and the dykes and shoreworks of Fengcheng and neighboring counties. The people reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 嘗上奏，不具齎奏人姓名，吏科論其簡恣。

translations.literal: Once when submitting a memorial he did not include the name of the bearer; the Personnel Branch supervising secretaries criticized him for being perfunctory and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he submitted a memorial without naming the bearer; the Personnel Branch supervising secretaries impeached him for perfunctory and disrespectful conduct.

sentences.zh: 帝宥其罪，錄彈章示之。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned his offense and had the impeachment memorial copied and shown to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned the offense and had the impeachment memorial copied and shown to him.

sentences.zh: 遂乞休歸。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested retirement and went home.

sentences.zh: 僦居民舍，布政使張瓚為築西湖書院居之。

translations.literal: He rented a civilian dwelling; the provincial administration commissioner Zhang Zan built West Lake Academy for him to live in.
translations.idiomatic: He rented a house from a local resident, and the provincial administration commissioner Zhang Zan built West Lake Academy for him to live in.

sentences.zh: 家食三十年，年近九十而卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home on his pension for thirty years and died nearing ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for thirty years and died near the age of ninety.

sentences.zh: 時正雅好學。

translations.literal: Shizheng was by nature fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shizheng was by nature devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 閒居久，多所著述，于稽古禮文事尤詳。

translations.literal: During his long retirement he wrote extensively, and was especially thorough in matters of classical research and ritual texts.
translations.idiomatic: During his long retirement he wrote extensively, and was especially learned in classical research and matters of ritual.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金純等黽勉奉公，當官稱職。

translations.literal: The historian comments: Jin Chun and the others strove diligently in public service and fulfilled their duties in office.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Jin Chun and the others strove diligently in public service and proved equal to their offices.

sentences.zh: 加之禔躬清白，操行無虧，固列卿之良也。

translations.literal: Add to this pure personal conduct and unblemished character — they were indeed fine exemplars among the ranks of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Add to this personal purity and unblemished conduct, and they were truly fine exemplars among the ranks of ministers.

sentences.zh: 鄭辰之廉事，周瑄之治獄，皆有仁人之用心，君子哉。

translations.literal: Zheng Chen's integrity in office, Zhou Xuan's governance of legal cases — both show the concern of humane men. True gentlemen indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chen's integrity in office and Zhou Xuan's handling of legal cases both reveal the heart of humane men. True gentlemen, every one.
